areas.title: Abstract Management (Review Depth & Disposition)

items.reasoning: The clone has an 'Evaluation plans' concept where each plan is an independent round with its own name, opens/closes dates and its own scoring criteria. The reloaded plans list (image 20) shows 'Initial Review' 1 Aug 2026 – 15 Oct 2026 (OPEN NOW) and 'Final Review' 16 Oct 2026 – 30 Nov 2026 (OPENS 16 OCT 2026) alongside pre-seeded plans. Scorecards visibly differ: Initial Review carries Relevance/Originality/Recommendation/Comments (S2 turns 15-20, confirmed later in the reviewer form and organizer review expansion, image 35), while Final Review carries 'Final Score' + 'Comments' on a 1–10 rating scale (images 17, 18). The Final Review plan page after creation (image 18) shows the persisted criteria, and the reviewer/organizer views in ABS-S3 (a separate session) still show Initial Review's criteria, proving persistence across reloads.

Reviewer membership is scoped inside each plan: the Initial Review plan page has a 'WHO REVIEWS WHAT' section listing sbek-reviewer@example.com (Sam Whitfield) attached to that plan with two specific submissions (image 15), while the newly-created Final Review plan shows its own separate 'WHO REVIEWS WHAT · Assign a reviewer' section with nothing attached (image 18) and the plans list reports Final Review as 'No evaluations assigned yet' vs Initial Review '0 of 2 evaluations in' (image 20). Sam's reviewer dashboard also lists progress per plan ('Across two open plans', 'Initial Review 2 assigned'), confirming per-round scoping rather than a single global reviewer pool.

The scorecard editor supports numeric criteria with a rating scale (Relevance, Originality, scale 1–5), a choice criterion (Recommendation with options Accept/Maybe/Reject, built in S2 turns 16-18) and a free-text criterion (Comments, image 15 shows the Comments row with a 'Required' toggle). On the reviewer side all three rendered and were filled (Relevance=2, Originality=4, Recommendation=Accept, comment text; S3 turns 14-18), submission succeeded ('1 of 2 done', queue row 'SES-031 SCORED 3.3'), values persisted on reopening the review (turn 24), and the organizer's expanded review shows all four stored values including the dropdown choice and comment text (image 31, image 35).

The scorecard editor has an explicit WEIGHT column with a computed percentage per criterion (33%/33%/33% by default; agent set Originality weight 2 / Relevance weight 1 giving 67%/33% — S2 turn 15-16, weights visible in images 16-18). The results table is headed 'SCORES AVERAGE BY WEIGHT · RECUSALS EXCLUDED' and shows 3.3 for 'Taming 40-Minute CI' from scores 2 and 4, i.e. (2*1+4*2)/3 = 3.33 rather than the plain average 3.0, exactly the weighted arithmetic the rubric predicts. The agent recorded this arithmetic explicitly.
evidence_refs: obs: Results aggregation confirmed for round-scoped 'Initial Review' plan: Taming 40-Minute CI shows Score=3.3 (weighted mean ...)

items.reasoning: The organizer assigned exactly two submissions to Sam Whitfield (image 15: sbek-reviewer@example.com → SES-031 'Taming 40-Minute CI' and SES-002 'Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You'). Signing in as the reviewer, the Initial Review queue showed '2 left to score' with only those two items and the agent explicitly confirmed 'Docs That Answer Back' was not listed (turn 7), despite 32 submissions existing in the event. The reviewer's navigation is restricted to /admin/review only.
evidence_refs: obs: Submissions list confirms 32 total submissions seeded

items.reasoning: The 'WHO REVIEWS WHAT' panel offers scale tooling: a 'Cap per reviewer [5] talks each' field, a 'Distribute the unassigned' auto-distribution button with a live readout ('32 talks · 32 reviews needed at 1 each · 0 reviewers'), plus a track filter dropdown ('AI Engineering') and a one-submission/bulk selector next to the Assign action (image 15). The agent used this panel to create the two assignments successfully ('Assign a reviewer applies immediately'; assignment rows present, later confirmed in the reviewer queue). Gap: the evidence does not show the 'Distribute the unassigned' auto-distribute button actually being clicked and completing, so only the cap/track-filtered assignment path is demonstrably exercised — but that alone satisfies the criterion's disjunction.

A per-plan anonymization setting exists ('Hide speaker names from reviewers — Reviewers see the abstract and track only', visible in the plan editor images 16-18) and the agent checked it for Initial Review (S2 turn 15). On the reviewer side the agent scanned the full blinded review page for 'Taming 40-Minute CI' and recorded that no author name, co-author name or company appeared, with explicit UI text 'The speaker's name and company are hidden while this plan is anonymised' (turn 10-11). The organizer view of the same submission shows 'Priya Raman · Latticework Systems · Principal Engineer' and Marcus Okafor in the participants/results rows (images 33, 28). Confidence is medium only because the blinded reviewer screenshot (007) was not attached for direct inspection; the transcript observation is explicit.

The per-plan 'Reviewer progress' dashboard showed Sam Whitfield '0 of 2 · NOT STARTED' before any reviews (image 22, ABS-S2), and after both evaluations were submitted the same dashboard showed 'Sam Whitfield · 2 of 2 · DONE' with 'Remind laggards (0)' (image 37, ABS-S3). Counts match actual review state and update live.

The progress view exposes bulk nudge actions targeting outstanding reviewers: 'Remind laggards (1)' and 'Remind the 1 not started' (image 22). Triggering it produced a success toast 'Sent: 1. Skipped: 0. Remaining: 0.' (image 23) and a Comms History entry 'Reminder: Initial Review review queue — 1 sent' at 16 Aug 20:48 (image 25). After the reviews completed the control correctly reads 'Remind laggards (0)' (image 37).

The 'Results: Initial Review' table shows a per-submission aggregate SCORE column with a review-count expander; descending order lists SES-002 'Your AI Pair Programmer' 5.0 at rank 1 and SES-031 'Taming 40-Minute CI' 3.3 at rank 2, above the unreviewed 0.0 rows (image 28). Toggling the sort reverses the ordering correctly: ascending puts the 0.0 rows first and the scored rows last at positions 31 (3.3) and 32 (5.0) of 32 (images 29, 30). Aggregates are consistent with the entered scores. One cosmetic oddity: the RANK column renumbers 1..n by display order, so in ascending mode the lowest-scored talk is labelled 'rank 1'.

Speaker side: the edit view's 'ON THIS SESSION (2)' list shows 'Priya Raman — SPEAKER' and 'Marcus Okafor — CO-PRESENTER' after saving, and the submission detail reads 'With Marcus Okafor (co-presenter)' (images 7, 13). Organizer side: the results table SPEAKER column for SES-031 lists 'Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor' (image 28), the Comms recipient picker shows both names on the submission (image 24), and the organizer submission detail has a participants table with PARTICIPANT / ROLE / EMAIL columns plus the note '1 speaker on this session are not on the public site yet' (image 34). Roles persist with labels on both sides.

A recusal control exists in the reviewer's scoring view: the agent recorded a checkbox labelled 'Recuse me from this one' directly above the Submit/Save buttons, scoped to that single submission (obs + turn 13). Corroborating UI text elsewhere: the assignment panel states 'A reviewer never sees a talk they are recused from' (image 15) and the results header reads 'SCORES AVERAGE BY WEIGHT · RECUSALS EXCLUDED' (image 28), showing the concept is wired into assignment and aggregation. The control was deliberately not exercised, so the flagged/removed outcome is unverified, but the rubric's pass condition (presence with wording recorded) is met. Confidence medium because screenshot 008 was not attached for direct inspection.
evidence_refs: obs: Conflict-of-interest control found: a checkbox labeled "Recuse me from this one"

items.reasoning: Export controls exist in the review area: 'Download CSV' on the plan results page (images 28, 38) and 'Export results CSV' on the Review plans index (image 20), plus 'Export CSV' in Comms history. The agent triggered the results Download CSV link (pointing at /api/v1/plans/{id}/results?format=csv&round=1); the click produced no error and did not navigate away, consistent with a Content-Disposition download. Gap named: no in-app confirmation toast or filename was rendered and the downloaded file's contents could not be inspected, so only the UI-observable half is verified.
evidence_refs: obs: Export control: 'Download CSV' link at /admin/review/plans/{id}/results ...

items.reasoning: Nothing in any captured surface claims or provides AI-assisted triage: the plan editor (criteria, weights, rating scale, anonymization) has no AI evaluator option, the reviewer queue and scoring form contain only human criteria, and the results table's reviews expander attributes every score to a human reviewer ('Sam Whitfield ... Initial Review · Round 1') with no AI-vs-human distinction or AI rationale text. Per the rubric, absent an AI claim the item is not applicable; no AI feature was found. Note the agent did not record an explicit dedicated search, so a hidden AI feature cannot be fully excluded.

defects.description: On the organizer submission-detail page, the free-text 'Comments' from the Initial Review evaluation is duplicated onto a different plan's review entry ('Late-Stage Program Review', score 4.0), which has entirely different criteria (Content quality & depth, Speaker delivery & clarity, Recommendation: Approve). The comment shown under that second review is verbatim the Initial Review comment, misattributing reviewer feedback across evaluation plans.

In the results table the RANK column simply renumbers rows by display order, so after toggling to ascending score sort the lowest-scored (0.0) submission is labelled 'rank 1' and the top-scored 5.0 talk is 'rank 32'. The rank number is therefore misleading in ascending mode.

Duplicate submissions with identical titles coexist with divergent states: 'Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You: Verification Patterns That Scale' appears as SES-032 (Priya Raman, Declined, 0 reviews) and SES-002 (Marcus Okafor, pending, reviewed), which makes the reviewer queue / results ambiguous about which record is authoritative.
Triggering 'Download CSV' from the results page yields no in-app feedback whatsoever (no toast, no filename, no state change), leaving the organizer unsure whether the export succeeded.

areas.notes: Both organizer-side scenarios (ABS-S2, ABS-S3) ended on the 70-turn limit rather than a natural finish, and several key screenshots (round-1 scorecard editor 008, blinded reviewer view 007, recuse control 008, reviewer queue 005) were not attached for direct inspection — for those items I relied on the transcript/observations, which are detailed and internally consistent with the attached screenshots (e.g. the stored 2/4/Accept/comment values later visible in the organizer's expanded review). Despite the turn limits, every rubric-relevant state was reached at least once, so no item required cannot_judge. The clone's model is 'evaluation plans' where each plan = an independent round carrying its own dates, rating scale, weighted criteria, anonymization flag, reviewer pool, progress view, results table and CSV export; this maps cleanly onto the multi-round review depth this spec grades.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker seeds submissions with a co-author
scenarios.summary:
Scenario ABS-S1 completed successfully.

1. Navigated to http://localhost:8890; found the public CFP already open (closes 30 Apr 2027, no need for the organizer-reopen precondition).
2. Signed in as the seeded speaker (sbek-speaker@example.com / SbekTest!2027-spk), who is Priya Raman - the account already existed from the chained area-01 run.
3. Speaker dashboard already contained all three target proposals from area 01 (reused, no duplicates created):
   - "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" - SES-031, Accepted, Talk/Platform & Infra
   - "Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You: Verification Patterns That Scale" - SES-032, Not accepted, Talk/AI Engineering
   - "Docs That Answer Back: Retrieval-Grounded Documentation Sites" - SES-003, Under review, Lightning Talk/Developer Experience
   (A fourth, unrelated seeded submission "Six Minutes, Not Forty..." also appeared, accepted.)
4. Opened "Taming 40-Minute CI" and used Edit submission → found a "Participants" / "On this session" section with an "Add a co-presenter" control (first name, last name, email, role dropdown: Co-presenter/Moderator/Panelist). Added Marcus Okafor (marcus.speaker@sbek-test.example.com) with role "Co-presenter". Screenshotted the filled co-presenter form before adding, then the resulting participants list before saving, then saved changes.
5. Verified persistence: the submission detail page now reads "With Marcus Okafor (co-presenter)", and the edit page's participants list shows "On this session (2)": Priya Raman - SPEAKER, Marcus Okafor - CO-PRESENTER — both with distinct role labels, screenshotted.
6. Screenshotted the speaker dashboard showing all submissions with status labels (Accepted / Not accepted / Under review).

All three SUCCESS SIGNALS were met: three (in fact four) submissions visible with status labels; submission detail/edit view shows both Priya Raman and Marcus Okafor each with a role label; screenshots captured of the co-author control filled and the saved state.

Observations recorded: the co-presenter add form only captures name/email/role (no title/company field), co-presenters are not emailed and are not shown on the public site until the organizer explicitly publishes them (a deliberate moderation gate, noted as expected behavior not a bug). No duplicate submissions were created since all three already existed from the prior chained scenario.
observations: ABS-S1 verified end-to-end. All three target proposals already existed from the chained area-01 run (no duplicates were created): 'Taming 40-Minute CI...' (SES-031, Accepted), 'Your AI Pair Programmer...' (SES-032, Not accepted), 'Docs That Answer Back...' (SES-003, Under review). A fourth seeded submission 'Six Minutes, Not Forty...' (SES-001, Accepted) also exists in the speaker's dashboard - likely unrelated seed data, not part of this scenario's three targets, but shown for completeness. Co-author control WAS FOUND: on the edit-submission page there is a 'Participants' section titled 'On this session' with an 'Add a co-presenter' form (First name, Last name, Email, Role dropdown with options Co-presenter/Moderator/Panelist). Added Marcus Okafor (marcus.speaker@sbek-test.example.com, would-be Staff Developer Advocate at Cloudreach Labs - title/company fields not offered on the co-presenter add form, only name/email/role) with role 'Co-presenter'. He appeared immediately in the 'On this session' list without needing to save (client-side add), and persisted after clicking 'Save changes' - the submission detail page now reads 'With Marcus Okafor (co-presenter)'. The participants list shows both: Priya Raman - SPEAKER, Marcus Okafor - CO-PRESENTER, confirming both appear with distinct role labels. Note: the UI explicitly states co-presenters are not emailed automatically and are not shown on the public site until the organizer publishes them - a deliberate privacy/moderation gate, not a bug. CFP was found open (closes 30 Apr 2027) so no organizer close-date-reopening precondition step was needed.

scenarios.scenarioName: Reviewer scores blind; organizer checks aggregates and export
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: Conflict-of-interest control found: a checkbox labeled "Recuse me from this one" appears directly above the Submit/Save buttons on the review view, scoped to this single submission. Left unchecked to avoid disrupting the review submission (recording presence/wording only, not clicking, since scenario guidance says only click if clearly reversible/scoped — this appears reversible as a plain checkbox but clicking would recuse Sam from scoring this required submission, which would block completing the scenario).

Results aggregation confirmed for round-scoped 'Initial Review' plan: Taming 40-Minute CI shows Score=3.3 (weighted mean of Relevance=2 (weight1) and Originality=4 (weight2) => (2*1+4*2)/3=3.33, rounded display 3.3), matching the scenario's predicted weighted average (~3.33) rather than plain average 3.0. This confirms the plan correctly weights Originality x2. The submission's own detail page (/admin/submissions/{id}) shows ALL reviews across ALL plans for that submission (2 of 6 in) — including the separate 'Late-Stage Program Review' plan's earlier all-4s-style review (Content quality & depth=4, Speaker delivery=4, Recommendation=Approve, score 4.0) — but the Initial Review results table correctly scopes its aggregate to only the 1 review submitted within that plan/round (3.3), i.e. it does NOT pool the other plan's review into this round's aggregate. Minor UI bug observed: the submission-detail page displays the same 'Comments' text under both review entries (the Initial-Review comment text is duplicated onto the Late-Stage-Program-Review entry), even though that entry's own criteria (content quality/speaker delivery) differ — likely a stale/shared-comment rendering bug, not a scoring error.

Export control: 'Download CSV' link at /admin/review/plans/{id}/results points to /api/v1/plans/mefyn5gaxss5mk4eqfkv/results?format=csv&round=1 (a direct GET link, not a JS-triggered blob). Clicking it did not navigate away from the results page and produced no on-screen confirmation toast/dialog — consistent with the browser silently downloading a file via Content-Disposition, but no visible in-app confirmation or filename display was rendered. The URL implies filename/format via query params (format=csv&round=1) but no explicit filename was shown on-screen.

areas.title: AI Agenda & Schedule Builder

items.reasoning: The /admin/agenda builder renders a full grid: vertical time axis (9:00–17:30 in 30-min rows), room columns (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab, plus 'No room yet'), a day switcher with the three event days (Wed 12 / Thu 13 / Fri 14 May), an 'Unscheduled' pool sidebar with session cards, break rows (coffee break, lunch), and header stats (unplaced / conflicts / % placed). Sessions render as cards positioned by day/time/room with title, ref, speakers and track colouring. Day tabs are present and functional-looking controls in every builder screenshot; the agent did not explicitly click Thu/Fri, which is the only small evidence gap, but the day-navigation affordance and per-day rendering are clearly there.

Settings → 'Tracks and rooms' exposes creation UI for both. The four fixture rooms (Main Stage, Room 2A, Room 2B, Workshop Lab) exist and the agent created a new room 'Overflow Room' (seats 50); the list updated to 'ROOMS · 5' and, critically, the builder then rendered an 'Overflow Room' column as a schedulable location. A new track 'Community' was also created successfully (TRACKS · 4, 0 submissions) alongside the three pre-existing fixture tracks, and track labels are visibly attached to sessions (track chips on the submission detail 'TRACKS: AI Engineering', track colour bars on agenda cards, track chips on the public agenda, plus an 'All tracks' filter on Submissions).

SES-031 'UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI' was placed from the Unscheduled pool into Wed 12 May 10:00 in Room 2A; the card renders in that cell with its title and speakers and a toast confirmed 'Placed SES-031 in Room 2A at 10:00'. The Unscheduled count dropped 4→3. Persistence is confirmed: scenario AIA-S2 was a fresh login and fresh page load of /admin/agenda, where SES-031 still appears in Room 2A at 10:00 (header 89% placed, 2 unplaced), and it remains there through the later S2 screenshots. The dedicated in-scenario reload step was not reached, but the cross-session reload evidence is equivalent.

After Priya Raman was added as co-presenter on SES-002 and SES-002 was placed at Wed 10:00 in Room 2B while SES-031 (Priya Raman, Marcus Okafor) sat at Wed 10:00 in Room 2A, both cards immediately rendered a 'SPEAKER DOUBLE-BOOKED' badge with no manual refresh, and a toast reported 'Placed SES-002 in Room 2B at 10:00. 2 new clashes — flagged, not blocked.' The header conflict counter also incremented. The badge identifies the conflict type on the specific clashing session cards (which list the shared speakers).
evidence_refs: obs: Speaker double-booking detection WORKS ... BOTH session cards immediately displayed a black/white badge reading "SPEAKER DOUBLE-BOOKED"

items.reasoning: Placing SES-003 into the already-occupied Wed 10:00 / Room 2A cell (via drag-and-drop) was accepted rather than blocked — consistent with the app's stated policy 'CLASHES ARE FLAGGED, NOT BLOCKED' — and both cards in that cell then displayed a clearly visible 'ROOM & SPEAKER CONFLICT' badge, with a toast 'Placed SES-003 in Room 2A at 10:00. 4 new clashes — flagged, not blocked.' The rubric explicitly allows the flagged-not-blocked behaviour. Note the click-to-assign path to that occupied slot failed because the occupied card covers the slot button (recorded separately as a defect), but the room-conflict flagging itself works.
evidence_refs: obs: Room double-booking test ... both cards in that cell now display a "ROOM & SPEAKER CONFLICT" badge

items.reasoning: Moving works and persists: SES-002 was moved out of Room 2B 10:00 to Room 2B 14:00, the toast confirmed 'Placed SES-002 in Room 2B at 14:00', the card renders in the new 14:00 slot with no conflict badge, and it is still at 14:00 Room 2B on the fresh page load in AIA-S2 — so the previously flagged speaker double-booking on that card cleared after the move. However, the gap: the room conflict created in step 9 was never resolved (the agent hit the turn limit mid-placement of SES-003), so the header still reads '6 conflicts' and SES-003/SES-031 remain stacked in Room 2A 10:00 with the 'ROOM & SPEAKER CONFLICT' badge, both in S1's final state and on reload in S2. Full 'conflicts clear after resolving overlaps' is therefore only partially demonstrated (and the header counter did not visibly decrease after the successful move).

'Publish schedule' exists in the builder toolbar; clicking it entered a 'Publishing…' state and returned a success status 'Schedule live — 12 of 18 placed sessions are public. 6 held back: content not approved.' with an explicit held-back list rendered in-page. The attendee-facing surface at /e/devflow-conf-2027/agenda then renders Wednesday 12 May with day/time/room details and includes fixture sessions scheduled in this area (e.g. auto-placed SES-027 'Beyond the Hype: Monorepo Tooling in Practice' at 13:00 Main Stage, plus SES-011 and SES-010 at 14:00), confirming the handoff. Sessions gated by content approval are intentionally withheld, which is a deliberate reported behaviour rather than a publish failure; public rendering quality is out of scope here.
evidence_refs: obs: Publish action: 'Publish schedule' button in agenda toolbar ... 'Schedule live — 12 of 18 placed sessions are public.'

items.reasoning: An 'Auto-schedule' button sits in the agenda toolbar next to 'Publish schedule'. Triggering it showed a processing state then a success banner 'Auto-schedule placed 2 sessions. 0 unplaced. 6 pre-existing conflicts left in place.' The Unscheduled pool went from 2 items to 0 ('All accepted sessions are placed', 100% placed) and the two previously unscheduled sessions appear in the grid: SES-033 'Lightning: Agents in Production Q&A' at Room 2A 9:00 and SES-027 'Beyond the Hype…' at Main Stage 13:00, both without new conflict badges.
evidence_refs: obs: Auto-schedule control found: 'Auto-schedule' button in toolbar

defects.description: Click-to-assign cannot target a slot that already contains a session card: the occupied card overlays the underlying 'Place … at 10:00 in Room 2A' button, so the click-to-place flow silently fails there (drag-and-drop still works). A hit-target/z-index issue that makes intentional over-booking or re-stacking impossible via the keyboard/click path.
defects.where: /admin/agenda builder, occupied grid cell (Room 2A, Wed 12 May 10:00) — AIA-S1/screenshots/022-room2a-1000-slot-covered.jpg

defects.description: The header conflict counter's arithmetic is hard to reconcile with the per-action toasts (started at 2 conflicts; toasts reported +1, +2, +4 new clashes; counter read 5 per the agent then 6 after a move that removed a speaker overlap). The counter did not visibly decrease after a session was successfully moved out of an overlapping slot, which risks misleading organizers about resolution progress.
defects.where: /admin/agenda header stats ('N unplaced · N conflicts · N% placed') — AIA-S1/screenshots/025-conflict-counter-after-first-resolve.jpg vs. 024-after-move-attempt-1400.jpg

defects.description: The public agenda shows a scheduled session with room label 'TO BE ANNOUNCED' (SES-026 Developer Metrics at 11:00), i.e. a session placed in the builder's 'No room yet' column is published without a room. Not a hard failure but leaks incomplete scheduling state to attendees.

areas.notes: AIA-S1 ended with agent_error (70-turn limit) before its explicit reload-verification and second conflict-resolution move, so persistence and conflict-clearing had to be inferred from AIA-S2, which began with a fresh login and page load of /admin/agenda and showed the S1 placements intact (SES-031 in Room 2A 10:00, SES-002 in Room 2B 14:00, 6 conflicts, 89% placed). That cross-scenario reload is strong persistence evidence for AIA-03 but leaves AIA-06's 'conflicts clear' half-demonstrated: only the moved card's flag cleared, while the deliberately created room conflict was never unwound. Day navigation tabs (Wed/Thu/Fri) were visible in every builder screenshot but never clicked, so per-day rendering on Thu/Fri is unverified though structurally evident. The app's design choice is to flag rather than block clashes, stated explicitly in the builder header, which the rubric accepts for AIA-05. Publish is content-approval gated per session, so several fixture sessions (including the Lightning talk and Taming 40-Minute CI) were withheld from the public agenda by design; that is reported transparently and is not treated as a defect here.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build agenda structure, place sessions, trigger and resolve conflicts
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: Speaker double-booking detection WORKS: after placing SES-031 (Taming 40-Minute CI, speakers Priya Raman + Marcus Okafor) at Wed 12 May 10:00 in Room 2A, and then SES-002 (Your AI Pair Programmer, speakers Marcus Okafor + Priya Raman) at same day/time in Room 2B, BOTH session cards immediately displayed a black/white badge reading "SPEAKER DOUBLE-BOOKED" directly on the card in the grid. A toast/status message also appeared: "Placed SES-002 in Room 2B at 10:00. 2 new clashes — flagged, not blocked." The running conflict counter at the top also incremented (3 conflicts). This matches success signal: visible speaker double-booking warning while sessions overlap.

Room double-booking test: attempted to place SES-003 (Docs That Answer Back) at Day1 10:00 in Room 2A, same slot already occupied by SES-031 (Taming 40-Minute CI). Clicking the "Place SES-003 at 10:00 in Room 2A" button via the click-to-select flow failed because the occupied session card visually covers the underlying slot button (a minor z-index/hit-target UI issue), but drag-and-drop of the SES-003 card from Unscheduled onto the Room 2A/10:00 cell worked successfully. The placement was NOT blocked — it succeeded and both cards in that cell now display a "ROOM & SPEAKER CONFLICT" badge (combining the pre-existing speaker double-booking with the new room overlap). Toast read: "Placed SES-003 in Room 2A at 10:00. 4 new clashes — flagged, not blocked." This matches the app's stated policy shown in the header: "Clashes are flagged, not blocked." Conflict counter increased to 5.

scenarios.scenarioName: Auto-schedule assist and publish the agenda
scenarios.summary:
Signed in as organizer Jordan Alvarez and opened /admin/agenda for DevFlow Conf 2027. The agenda builder retained state from AIA-S1: grid was ~89% placed with 2 unplaced sessions in the sidebar pool, one of which was the target "Lightning: Agents in Production Q&A" (SES-033, Marcus Okafor) already existing from area 04's content upload — no manual creation was needed.

1) Auto-schedule control: found as an "Auto-schedule" button directly in the agenda toolbar next to "Publish schedule" (no need to search overflow menus). Screenshotted before/after.

2) Triggered auto-schedule: button went to a disabled/processing state, then returned a success banner: "Auto-schedule placed 2 sessions. 0 unplaced. 6 pre-existing conflicts left in place." Both previously-unscheduled sessions (SES-027 "Beyond the Hype: Monorepo Tooling in Practice" and SES-033 "Lightning: Agents in Production Q&A") were placed into clean, conflict-free slots (Main Stage 13:00 and Room 2A 9:00 respectively) — verified visually in the grid. The pre-existing 6 conflicts (double-bookings/room clashes from AIA-S1) were untouched by the auto-scheduler, confirming it only fills empty slots rather than resolving clashes.

3) Publish action: "Publish schedule" button in the toolbar. Clicking it showed a "Publishing..." transient disabled state, then a detailed result: "Schedule live — 12 of 18 placed sessions are public. 6 held back: content not approved," with an explicit list of the 6 held-back sessions (including the target Lightning talk, since its uploaded content hadn't been approved in the Content queue). This demonstrates the publish step is content-approval-gated per session, a real safeguard rather than a blind toggle.

4) Public/attendee agenda handoff: navigated to /e/devflow-conf-2027/agenda without needing organizer auth (public route). Confirmed the page renders Wednesday 12 May's published sessions with day/time/room details, including "Beyond the Hype: Monorepo Tooling in Practice" at 13:00 in Main Stage — matching the auto-scheduled placement. The dedicated banner screenshots were not attached, but the page outlines in the transcript document both states.

The organizer's detail view of the same submission shows the abstract ending with the identical sentence, and the reviewer scorecard also displays it.

items.reasoning: Role separation is convincingly demonstrated: signed in as Sam Whitfield the app shows a reviewer-only console (single 'Review' nav item, no Submissions/Speakers/Content/Agenda/Comms/Settings), direct navigation to /admin/submissions silently redirects back to his queue, and an out-of-queue scorecard URL returns 'That submission is not in your review queue.' The provisioning half was not exercised: Sam pre-existed as a seeded account, so no reviewer was actually created/invited with new credentials; the agent only noted that a 'New reviewer account (email)' field exists in the plan's 'Who reviews what' UI.

items.reasoning: As Sam Whitfield the scorecard accepted ratings computing an Overall of 4.0, a recommendation of Approve, and the fixture comment; after 'Submit and next' the reviewer dashboard flipped to 'Nothing left in your queue', '1 of 1 done' and the chip 'SES-031 SCORED 4.0'. The organizer's detail view of SES-031 shows the same rating 4.0 and the identical comment text from Sam Whitfield.
evidence_refs: obs: the organizer detail view shows a review by Sam Whitfield with rating 4.0 and comment text 'Strong practical content and a clear narrative arc...'

items.reasoning: The organizer used decision controls on both submission detail pages (Accept on SES-031, Decline on SES-032) and the submissions list then displayed both distinct statuses side by side ('SES-031 = Accepted', 'SES-032 = Declined'). Downstream artefacts corroborate the decisions: the Comms compose step filtered by 'Accepted' status to exactly SES-031, and a 'Decline Notification' was sent for the other. The list screenshot itself was not attached, so this rests on the transcript plus corroborating comms evidence.

The only speaker-dashboard evidence (CFP-S2) predates the accept/reject decisions and shows both proposals as 'UNDER REVIEW'. CFP-S4 hit the 70-turn limit before signing back in as Priya Raman, so no post-decision speaker view was captured. Propagation is untested, not shown absent.

Judging only the UI-observable half: a Comms compose wizard (Recipients → Template → Preview → Send) exists, offers 'Acceptance Notification' and 'Decline Notification' templates, filters recipients by decision status, and after sending reports 'SEND COMPLETE — 1 of 1 speakers were emailed' with template, subject line and 'Sent: Just now, by you'. The history log lists both dispatches ('Your talk has been accepted to DevFlow Conf 2027' and 'Update on your submission to DevFlow Conf 2027', 1 sent each). Actual delivery/body personalization is not auto-verified by design.

After acceptance, SES-031 'Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale' with speaker Priya Raman appears in the Agenda's Unscheduled tray and was then placed into Room 2A at 15:00 ('Placed SES-031 in Room 2A at 15.00'), and the admin Content record for the same session shows the title, 'Priya Raman · SES-031 · Wed 12 May 15:00–15:30, Room 2A' — all carried over with no re-typing. Minor gap: the track label 'Platform & Infra' is not visibly rendered on the agenda card or content page in the captured screenshots (it is carried on the underlying record, which is the same id kjfgleuojn5i3eyihtfs).

The close date was never moved into the past during either run (both organizer scenarios hit the turn limit first), so the speaker-side lock could not be tested. The only speaker edit evidence is from the open-CFP state, where editing worked and the page said 'You can change this until the form closes on Thu 29 Apr 2027'.

Multi-event support clearly exists in the UI: the admin header carries an event switcher ('DevFlow Conf 2027 ▾') and a 'New event' modal (Name/Slug/Starts/Ends/Time zone/Venue) was opened and filled with 'Forward Summit 2028'. However creation was never completed — the final captured state shows the modal still open with a 'Please fill out this field.' validation bubble, and no events list/switcher showing both events was ever captured. So co-existence of two events is unproven.

Because the second event was never successfully created (CFP-S1 ended at the New event modal with a validation error), no second-event submissions/abstracts area was ever visited, so cross-event scoping could not be observed either way.

defects.description: Deadline is displayed inconsistently across surfaces: the public submit portal and public sessions sidebar say 'closes Fri 30 Apr 2027, 23:59 PDT' while the org home card says 'CLOSES THU 29 APR' and the speaker edit page says 'You can change this until the form closes on Thu 29 Apr 2027' — an apparent off-by-one/timezone rendering bug in the close date.

The 'New event' modal blocked submission with a 'Please fill out this field.' validation bubble even though the Time zone field visibly contained 'America/New_York' (and Name, Slug, Starts, Ends, Venue were filled), preventing the second event from being created.

Reviewer assignment scoping is easy to over-grant: track-wide reviewer assignments living in multiple evaluation plans silently widen a reviewer's effective queue beyond what a 'One submission' assignment implies, so the organizer must hunt across plans to remove them (the agent had to delete two pre-existing track assignments to achieve the intended scope).
defects.where: Admin → Review → Evaluation plans → 'Who reviews what'

areas.notes: Two of the four scenarios (CFP-S1 organizer build/publish, CFP-S4 decisions/notify/close) exhausted the 70-turn limit before finishing, which is why CFP-04 (closed portal), CFP-13 (decision propagation to speaker), CFP-16 (edit lock after close) and CFP-18 (per-event data scoping) have no evidence and are marked cannot_judge rather than not_found — none of these were shown to be absent. Many of the most relevant CFP-S1/S3/S4 screenshots (builder with new fields, organizer submissions list with both decisions, submission detail) were not attached, so several verdicts lean on the agent's transcript page-outlines and observations, which were consistent across scenarios. The app's account model differs from the script (submit-first, account created via emailed password link) — noted as a design deviation, not a defect.

observations: Public CFP submission URL confirmed: http://localhost:8890/submit/devflow-conf-2027 . Status shown as "Open", closes 30 Apr 2027 23:59 America/Los_Angeles (258 days away from seeded "now"). Event details (DevFlow Conf 2027, 12-14 May 2027, Moscone West San Francisco CA) match fixtures exactly and were pre-seeded — no need to create the event. Tracks (AI Engineering, Platform & Infra, Developer Experience) and Formats (Keynote 45min, Talk 30min, Lightning Talk 10min, Workshop 120min, Panel 45min) were pre-seeded matching fixtures exactly. Added two custom fields via the form builder: "Key takeaway" (Short text, Required) and confirmed "Audience level" (Single choice: Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced) was already present as optional dropdown. Added conditional field "Workshop prerequisites" (Long text, optional) with visibility rule Format is "Workshop (120 min)" — the builder natively supports conditional/show-when logic via Field/Is/Value selectors.

Public CFP form validation: clicking "Submit this talk" with all fields empty triggers native HTML5 required-field validation — browser shows "Please fill out this field." tooltip on the Title input (first required field), preventing submission. This confirms required fields (Title, Abstract, Track, Format, Key takeaway) are enforced client-side even for logged-out/no-account submitters.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker drafts, submits, and edits proposals
scenarios.summary:
Scenario CFP-S2 completed successfully with all success signals verified.

Key findings:
1. **Public CFP form (/submit/devflow-conf-2027)**: No account creation is required upfront — the app creates the speaker's portal account implicitly via an emailed password-setup link after the first submission (a deviation from the script's assumed signup-first flow, but functionally equivalent to SessionBoard's "submit → account" pattern). Since the speaker email (sbek-speaker@example.com) was already a seeded account, submissions were immediately associated with Priya Raman's existing portal.

2. **Draft capability**: Confirmed present. "Save draft" button produced a "Draft saved — you can return later to finish and submit" banner. Navigating away to the homepage and back to the same URL auto-resumed the draft with banner "Resuming your saved draft from <timestamp>" and the title pre-filled — screenshotted both states.

3. **Required-field validation**: Attempting to submit with Abstract/Key-takeaway empty triggered native browser validation ("Please fill out this field.") — screenshotted.

4. **Track/Format/Audience-level controls**: Implemented as radio-button groups (not classic dropdowns) with all options visible without interaction. Selecting "Workshop (120 min)" revealed a conditional "Workshop prerequisites" textarea; switching to "Talk (30 min)" hid it again — both states screenshotted, confirming dynamic form logic equivalent to the scripted dropdown check.

5. **Full submission #1** ("Taming 40-Minute CI...", track Platform & Infra, format Talk 30 min, audience Intermediate, Priya's bio, key takeaway as specified) was filled and screenshotted, then submitted, producing a confirmation page: "SUBMITTED · SES-031 / That's in. Check your email." with explicit text "We've emailed a confirmation for '...' to sbek-speaker@example.com" — screenshotted.

6. **Submitter dashboard**: Logged into /portal with seeded speaker credentials; the "Your submissions" list on the portal home and at /portal/submissions showed the new submission with status label "Under review" (SES-031), alongside two pre-seeded submissions (SES-003 Under review, SES-001 Accepted) — screenshotted.

7. **Edit test**: Opened submission via "Edit submission," appended "Updated: now includes 2026 benchmark data." to the abstract, saved. Reloaded the submission detail page directly via URL — the appended sentence was still present, confirming server-side persistence — screenshotted before and after reload.

8. **Second submission** ("Your AI Pair Programmer...", track AI Engineering, format Talk 30 min, audience Advanced, specified key takeaway) was filled and submitted, producing confirmation SES-032.

9. **Final dashboard**: /portal/submissions screenshotted showing all four submissions with clear status labels: SES-032 (Under review), SES-031 (Under review), SES-003 (Under review), SES-001 (Accepted) — both newly-created proposals confirmed listed with statuses.

No missing capabilities were found in this scenario; the only deviation from the script was the account-creation model (implicit/post-submission rather than a distinct pre-submission signup step), which was noted as an observation rather than treated as a defect since it accomplishes the same end result.
observations: Public CFP form at /submit/devflow-conf-2027 does NOT require account creation upfront. Text: "New speaker? Create an account by submitting your talk below — we'll email you a link to set a password when you're done." So identity/account creation happens implicitly via submission + email, not a separate signup step. This differs from script step 2 expectation (create submitter account first). Proceeding to fill form directly as Priya Raman using her seeded email.

Confirmation page text: "SUBMITTED · SES-031 / That's in. Check your email. / You can edit this until Fri 30 Apr 2027, 23:59 PDT. / Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale — Platform & Infra · Talk (30 min) / We've emailed a confirmation for "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" to sbek-speaker@example.com. / You already have an account here. Log in to track it." This confirms confirmation email is sent (per app's own note, auditable in /admin/comms) and gives submission ID SES-031.

Full scenario walkthrough summary: (1) Public CFP form at /submit/devflow-conf-2027 requires NO account upfront — account/password is created implicitly via email after first submission (deviates from script's assumption of signup-first, but functionally equivalent). (2) Draft capability confirmed: "Save draft" button produces a "Draft saved" banner; navigating away and returning to /submit/devflow-conf-2027 auto-resumes the draft via a "Resuming your saved draft from <timestamp>" banner with title pre-filled — this appears to be cookie/session-based since no login was involved. (3) Required-field validation confirmed via native browser validation bubble "Please fill out this field." on empty Abstract when attempting submit. (4) Track/Format/Audience level are radio-button groups (not dropdowns) with all options visible without opening anything; selecting Workshop (120 min) revealed a conditional 'Workshop prerequisites' field, and switching to Talk (30 min) hid it again — confirming dynamic form logic. (5) Full first proposal submitted successfully producing confirmation page 'That's in. Sam Whitfield (sbek-reviewer@example.com) was already a seeded reviewer account, so no new-account/invite flow was exercised (a 'New reviewer account (email)' field exists for that purpose but wasn't needed here — noted as an observation). Screenshot of the assignment screen shows Sam mapped to exactly one submission, distinct from the other reviewers' track-wide rows.
5. Signed out, signed in as reviewer Sam Whitfield via fixture credentials.

Reviewer dashboard showed exactly one item in queue ('1 left to score' → SES-031 'Taming 40-Minute CI'), with only a single 'Review' nav link and no admin navigation (Submissions/Speakers/Content/Agenda/Comms/Settings absent). (screenshot captured). Also tried navigating directly to /admin/submissions as reviewer — silently redirected back to reviewer's own queue, confirming no admin-page leak.
7. Set both ratings to 4 (computed Overall 4.0), chose 'Approve', entered the exact fixture comment. Screenshot of filled scorecard captured, then submitted via 'Submit and next'.

(3) IMPORTANT FINDING: seed data had Sam Whitfield already broadly assigned by TRACK (AI Engineering in one plan, Platform & Infra in another) across multiple evaluation plans, which would have given him access to the 'AI Pair Programmer' (AI Engineering) submission too. To honor the scenario's explicit 'ONLY Taming 40-Minute CI, not AI Pair Programmer' requirement, I removed Sam's two pre-existing track-wide assignments (a 'Remove' action per plan, with a confirmation dialog noting 'Scores they have already submitted stay') and then used the assignment scope selector's 'One submission' option (Reviewer/Assignment scope/Track/Submission dropdowns) to assign him ONLY SES-031 in the 'Late-Stage Program Review' plan. This scope option is a genuine per-submission assignment capability. (4) Reviewer dashboard (same /admin console, role-scoped) for Sam showed exactly one plan and one item: 'SES-031 NOT SCORED - Taming 40-Minute CI'; nav bar only showed a single 'Review' link, no admin nav items (no Submissions/Speakers/Content/Agenda/Comms/Settings). (5) Attempted URL-swap to reach the unassigned AI Pair Programmer submission's scorecard (/admin/review/plans/seed_evaluation_plan_0003/submissions/3wxqvwnmxf7ghfl4xim4) — server correctly blocked with 'That submission is not in your review queue.' Also tried navigating straight to /admin/submissions as the reviewer — it silently redirected back to the reviewer's own review queue, confirming no admin-list access leak. (6) Scorecard had 2 rated criteria (Content quality & depth weight 71%, Speaker delivery & clarity weight 29%) plus a non-averaged Recommendation radio (Approve/Maybe/Deny) and a free-text comment box. Set both criteria to 4 (Overall computed 4.0), chose 'Approve', entered the fixture comment verbatim, and submitted successfully via 'Submit and next'. (7) Post-submit, dashboard flipped to 'Nothing left in your queue. Nicely done.' with '1 of 1 done' and item chip 'SES-031 SCORED 4.0' plus a 'Change your score' edit link — a clear completed state.

areas.title: Content Management & Speaker Deliverables

items.reasoning: Both file-request tasks were created with name, instructions, due date, kind=Upload and assignment to "Everyone accepted (16)": the filled forms show "Upload Session Presentation" / "Final slide deck as a PDF, 16:9 aspect ratio." / May 1, 2027 and "Upload Final Headshot (print quality)" / April 14, 2027, with a "Task created." toast. The Speakers tracking dashboard afterwards shows both new columns with DUE 1 MAY 2027 and DUE 14 APR 2027 and PENDING status for Priya Raman and for the account-linked Marcus Okafor row, and across the full roster.

Priya's portal lists "Upload Final Headshot (print quality) (required) Due Wed 14 Apr 2027" and "Upload Session Presentation (required) Due Sat 1 May 2027" with To do status and Upload file buttons. After uploading the slides.pdf fixture the app returned a status banner ("Received your file for 'Upload Session Presentation'"), the task flipped to DONE, and the file is shown as "slides.pdf (version 1, uploaded Sun 16 Aug 2026, 18:09 PDT)" with the session selector bound to SES-031.

Portal views show only Priya's own submissions/sessions (e.g. SES-032 in "Your submissions"), with the agent explicitly recording that no Marcus Okafor (speaker2) data appeared anywhere in the speaker-scoped views. Direct navigation to /admin and /admin/comms redirected to /portal?from=admin with the banner "The organizer dashboard isn't part of your speaker portal — this is your home.", and /organizer returned a 404. No admin capability was exposed to the speaker session.
evidence_refs: obs: Admin route access control verified ... no admin/organizer content was ever exposed

items.reasoning: After the second upload via "Replace file", the speaker-side VERSION HISTORY lists v1 slides.pdf (18:09:24 PDT) and v2 slides.pdf (18:09:55 PDT) with v2 marked CURRENT, and both entries are individual download links, so the earlier version remains accessible rather than overwritten. Organizer side corroborates: the aggregate files library shows the slides.pdf row at V2, and the per-session file detail was observed showing 2 versions with newest/replaced markers.

Speaker-side comment thread shows "Priya Raman — Sun 16 Aug 2026, 18:09 PDT / Draft deck - final version coming Friday." attached to the slides.pdf deliverable. From the organizer account the same thread was observed on the same file ("Priya Raman (Speaker) v1 · 2 minutes ago Draft deck - final version coming Friday.") and the organizer's reply was posted with a "Sent to 1 recipient" confirmation. Confidence is medium because the organizer-side thread screenshots (014/016) are described in the transcript but not attached for direct inspection.

Explicit constraint text sits directly in the upload control area: for the presentation deliverable "Allowed types: .pdf, .ppt, .pptx, .key, .odp, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif, .txt, .md. Max 25 MB (8 MB for images)." and for the headshot "Allowed types: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif. Max 8 MB."

A per-speaker per-task matrix dashboard exists with due dates and PENDING/COMPLETE/OVERDUE states, all-pending for the new tasks in S1, and filters demonstrably change the set (search by name narrowed to "Showing 1 of 16"/"2 of 16"; "Overdue only" gave "Showing 14 of 16 speakers · overdue"). However the S3 evidence does not show Priya's presentation task actually flipped to complete on the dashboard: her filtered dashboard screenshots were not attached and the attached S3 dashboard rows (Toni/Xan/Alex/Elliot) only show other speakers still PENDING. Only indirect signals exist (open-task count dropped 51→50; Priya's speaker page shows 2 outstanding), so the "reflects uploads" half is unverified.

UI-observable half is satisfied: the deliverables dashboard exposes "Remind all outstanding" (plus per-speaker "Remind X" and "Remind this task" actions and a "skips anyone reminded in the last hour" note). Invoking it opened a "Review reminders" dialog listing 15 recipients with a draft template, and after sending the UI showed a "Sent to 15 contacts" confirmation toast. Actual delivery is out of scope. Confidence medium because the dialog/toast screenshots are described in the transcript but not attached.

The submission detail edit form (title + abstract) was used and the reloaded session detail shows the title "UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" and the abstract ending "...This session now includes a live demo of remote build caching." The new title also propagates to list surfaces (Priya's speaker page lists "SES-031 · UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI..."), confirming persistence beyond the edit form.

Bio editing works and persists: the contact drawer's PROFILE > BIO field was edited and Priya's speaker record afterwards shows the appended sentence "Priya leads the developer-productivity group at Latticework Systems." appended to her original bio. The headshot half is not evidenced: her record still renders a plain placeholder avatar in the before and after screenshots, and no photo-upload control or uploaded headshot.png is visible anywhere in the captured admin editor (the scenario ended at the turn limit on /admin/contacts).

The session detail HISTORY panel shows timestamped, attributed entries: "16 Aug, 21:12:34 Edited by Jordan Alvarez — Title and description changed" and "16 Aug, 21:12:57 Edited by Jordan Alvarez — Description changed", i.e. at least two distinct entries. After restore, the abstract retains the first edit's sentence ("...now includes a live demo of remote build caching.") but the second edit's sentence ("Attendees should bring a laptop.") is gone, and the restore itself is logged as a new entry at 21:13:13 by Jordan Alvarez.

A per-session content review status clearly exists and persists: Priya's speaker page shows SES-001 as "ACCEPTED · APPROVED" versus SES-031 as "ACCEPTED · PENDING" after her upload, there is a dedicated "Review the content ›" surface (/admin/content) with reviewer note/approve actions, and the speaker-side upload banner states "The session is off the public schedule pending the producer's approval." However the organizer never demonstrably set the status to approved and no public agenda/preview surface was checked, so the actual exclusion of unapproved content from public output is unverified (the scenario hit the turn limit and no deferral observation was recorded).

The Content > Files library aggregates 23 uploads with metadata and type filters; the slides.pdf row shows speaker "Priya Raman · 16 Aug, 21:09", session "SES-031 UPDATED: Taming 40-Minute CI...", version V2, size and a Download link — consistent with the two uploads made in S2. A per-session file detail view showing the same file with its 2 versions and comment thread was also observed.

A bulk ZIP export affordance exists in the files library ("Download all 23 (.zip)" alongside type filters Slides·18 / Poster·1 / Headshot·4 that can narrow the set), which is positive evidence for the UI half. But no multi-select controls (per-row checkboxes) are visible in the captured library, the export was never invoked, and no grouping dialog or generation/queued/ready confirmation was observed — the organizer scenario ended at the turn limit before this step.

defects.description: Marcus Okafor appears as two separate contact rows on the deliverables dashboard: a placeholder "INVITED" row with all task cells blank and the message "Invited - not confirmed yet. Confirm participation to assign this event's tasks.", and an account-linked row carrying the tasks. This duplicate identity makes per-speaker deliverable tracking ambiguous (Contacts also reports "4 possible duplicates").

Task assignment/participation state is inconsistent: the account-linked Marcus Okafor row is labelled "NOT INVITED" for participation yet has the new upload tasks assigned as PENDING, while the sibling "INVITED" row claims tasks cannot be assigned until participation is confirmed.
defects.where: /admin/speakers task tracker rows for Marcus Okafor (CNT-S1/016-marcus-tasks-tracking.jpg)

defects.description: No dedicated file-collection enablement setting exists; the Speaker portal settings page exposes only an onboarding-task counter, so organizers must infer that creating a Kind=Upload task is the mechanism for requesting deliverables.

areas.notes: S1 and S2 completed cleanly and provide strong, directly-inspectable evidence for task creation, the speaker portal upload/versioning/comment flow, upload constraints, and speaker scoping/route blocking. S3 (organizer tracking/review/approve/export) hit the 70-turn harness limit partway through, and several of its early screenshots (dashboard filtered views, reminder dialog/toast, organizer comment thread, files library row) were captured but not attached — those are judged from the transcript descriptions where explicit. Consequently three items are under-evidenced through no fault of the app: the dashboard's reflection of Priya's completed presentation task (CNT-07), the headshot photo upload (CNT-10), the approval gate against a public surface (CNT-12), and the multi-select ZIP export invocation (CNT-14). None of these gaps were shown to be broken behaviour, only unverified.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer sets up content collection
scenarios.summary:
Completed the CNT-S1 scenario against Chautauqua (the Chautauqua app implements SessionBoard-like CFP/speaker management).

1. Logged in as organizer Jordan Alvarez via seeded demo-account button at /login → /admin/overview. Seeded event "DevFlow Conf 2027" (12–14 May 2027, Moscone West SF) already existed at slug devflow-conf-2027; confirmed details in Settings > Event. Multi-event support: a "Switch event" control exists in the header (not exercised further, out of scope for this scenario).

2. Verified/created the two distinct-speaker accepted sessions required:
   - Priya Raman: SES-031 "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" already existed, Accepted, track Platform & Infra, format Talk (30m) — reused as instructed.
   - Marcus Okafor: SES-032 "Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You…" was confirmed to already belong to Priya Raman with a Declined decision — left untouched per instructions. Created a NEW submission SES-033 "Lightning: Agents in Production Q&A" (Lightning Talk 10 min, track AI Engineering) with speaker name Marcus Okafor / email sbek-speaker2@example.com via Submissions > New submission, then set its decision to Accepted. Screenshotted the submissions list showing both accepted, distinct-speaker sessions (SES-031, SES-033) plus the untouched Declined SES-032.

3. Located the file-collection/deliverables feature: it lives under the "Speakers" admin tab (task tracker) rather than a separate Settings > Files toggle. Settings > Speaker portal shows a running "Onboarding tasks: N tasks · created when a submission is accepted" counter but no dedicated files-enabled switch — creating a Task with Kind=Upload is the functional equivalent of "enabling file uploads." Recorded this as an explicit observation (no standalone toggle exists).

4. Created task 1 via Speakers > New task: Task="Upload Session Presentation", Instructions="Final slide deck as a PDF, 16:9 aspect ratio.", Due date=1 May 2027, Kind=Upload, Deliverable kind=Presentation, Required, Assign to="Everyone accepted (16)". Screenshotted the filled form before saving (shows name+instructions+due date together). Saved successfully ("Task created").

5. Created task 2: Task="Upload Final Headshot (print quality)", Due date=14 Apr 2027, Kind=Upload, Deliverable kind=Photo/headshot, Required, Assign to="Everyone accepted (16)". Screenshotted filled form; saved successfully.

6. Verified the tracking dashboard (Speakers page) now lists both new task columns for all 16 accepted speakers, each showing due date and "Pending" status. Filtered/searched to Priya Raman and Marcus Okafor individually and screenshotted each: both show "Upload Final Headshot (print quality)" (due 14 Apr 2027, Pending) and "Upload Session Presentation" (due 1 May 2027, Pending). Note: Marcus Okafor appeared as two contact rows — one linked account (sbek-speaker2@example.com, 'has account') showing all 10 tasks Pending including the 2 new ones, and one placeholder 'Invited' row from an earlier co-presenter-style seed relationship with limited fields; the account-linked row is the authoritative one and carries both new tasks correctly.

7. Cross-verified end-to-end by logging in as the real speaker (sbek-speaker@example.com / Priya Raman) and viewing /portal: her 'Waiting on you' task list explicitly shows 'Upload Final Headshot (print quality) (required), Due Wed 14 Apr 2027' and 'Upload Session Presentation (required), Due Sat 1 May 2027' with working 'Upload file' buttons — confirming the organizer-created tasks correctly propagate to the speaker-facing portal.

All three success signals were satisfied: (a) filled task-creation form screenshots showing name/instructions/due date for the slides task, (b) tracking dashboard showing both tasks for both target speakers with due dates and incomplete/pending status (plus full-roster view of all 16 speakers x both new tasks), (c) documented that no separate 'file-uploads-enabled' toggle exists — task creation with Kind=Upload is the substitute mechanism, called out explicitly as a product observation rather than papered over.
observations: No standalone 'enable file uploads' toggle exists (unlike SessionBoard's Sessions > Settings > Files). Instead, file-collection is achieved by creating a Task with Kind=Upload (as done for both tasks). Settings > Speaker portal correctly reflects the running total: 'Onboarding tasks 10 tasks · created when a submission is accepted' (was 8 before this scenario, +2 for the two new tasks), confirming the tasks are wired into the speaker portal onboarding flow.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker uploads and versions a deliverable
scenarios.summary:
Full scenario executed successfully against the Chautauqua speaker portal for Priya Raman.

1. Signed in at /login using seeded speaker credentials (sbek-speaker@example.com); landed on /portal.
2. Screenshotted the pre-upload task list ("4 things to do") showing "Upload Final Headshot (print quality)" (due Wed 14 Apr 2027, To do) and "Upload Session Presentation" (due Sat 1 May 2027, To do) alongside other onboarding tasks (Hotel stay form - overdue, Announce participation).
3. Opened /portal/tasks (full task list). Before uploading, recorded stated file constraints for the presentation task: "Allowed types: .pdf, .ppt, .pptx, .key, .odp, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif, .txt, .md. Max 25 MB (8 MB for images)." Also noted headshot constraints: "Allowed types: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif. Max 8 MB." Selected the SES-031 "Taming 40-Minute CI" session from the per-task session dropdown before uploading (task screenshot captured).
4. Uploaded fixture slides.pdf against the Upload Session Presentation task. Task flipped to DONE status; filename "slides.pdf (version 1, uploaded ...)" recorded; status banner confirmed receipt and noted the session is pulled from the public schedule pending producer review.
5. Added comment "Draft deck - final version coming Friday." on the uploaded file. Comment rendered with author "Priya Raman" and timestamp "Sun 16 Aug 2026, 18:09 PDT" — screenshotted.
6. Re-uploaded slides.pdf to the same deliverable slot via "Replace file". Version history list now shows v1 (Sun 16 Aug 2026, 18:09:24 PDT) and v2 (Sun 16 Aug 2026, 18:09:55 PDT) with v2 explicitly labeled "CURRENT". Screenshotted the full version list alongside the retained comment.
7. No separate "mark complete" control exists for upload-type tasks — uploading auto-transitions the task to DONE (observed and recorded as a product behavior note). Left "Upload Final Headshot" deliberately untouched; it remained in "To do" status with its due date (Wed 14 Apr 2027) throughout.
8. Scoping check: browsed /portal and /portal/tasks — only Priya Raman's own 4 submissions and 2 sessions ever appeared; no trace of Marcus Okafor (speaker2) data anywhere. Attempted direct navigation to /admin and /admin/comms — both redirected to /portal?from=admin with an explicit on-page banner: "The organizer dashboard isn't part of your speaker portal — this is your home." /organizer returned a clean 404 "That page isn't here" page. No admin content was ever exposed.
9. Final portal screenshot confirms: Upload Session Presentation = DONE with 2-version slides.pdf (v2 current) and a retained comment; Upload Final Headshot = still To do, due Wed 14 Apr 2027.

All success signals were verified: pre-upload task list with due dates/status, post-upload state with filename recorded, two-version list with latest flagged, comment with author/timestamp, and confirmed admin-route inaccessibility for the speaker account.
observations: The 'Upload Session Presentation' task automatically transitions to DONE status upon file upload - there is no separate explicit 'mark complete' button for this task type (unlike the 'Announce participation' task which does have a 'Mark complete' button). This is an implicit completion model tied to the upload action itself, which satisfies script step 7's intent (task shows complete) even though there's no separate action to invoke.

Admin route access control verified: /admin and /admin/comms both redirect speaker account to /portal?from=admin with explicit banner message "The organizer dashboard isn't part of your speaker portal — this is your home." /organizer returns a 404 'That page isn't here' page. No admin/organizer content was ever exposed to the speaker session. Additionally, browsing the portal (dashboard, tasks, submissions) shows ONLY Priya Raman's own 4 submissions and 2 sessions - no trace of Marcus Okafor (speaker2) data appeared anywhere in the speaker-scoped views, confirming proper data scoping per-speaker account.

scenarios.scenarioName: Non-admin tour of the four browse widgets
scenarios.summary:
Completed the non-admin tour of all four (five, counting embeds) public browse widgets for DevFlow Conf 2027 entirely as an anonymous, logged-out visitor — no organizer/admin/attendee credentials were ever needed or used.

Findings:
- Homepage (http://localhost:8890/) lists the event with no login and links to the public site at /e/devflow-conf-2027/{sessions,speakers,agenda,gallery} plus a public CFP at /submit/devflow-conf-2027 and an embed family at /embed/devflow-conf-2027/<surface>.
- Content was NOT gated behind the area-04 approval precondition in this run: 12 sessions across 3 days and 12 speakers were visible immediately, so the organizer-login/approve-everything workaround in step 2 was not needed (explicitly recorded).
- SESSIONS LIST: verified result framing ('N of 12 sessions'), captured full-page screenshot, and audited 3 cards for title/description/date+time/room/speaker(name+title+company)/Format tag/Track tag — all present. One card showed 'To be announced' for an unset room, handled gracefully. Show-more expand/collapse demonstrated with before/after screenshots.
- SESSIONS SEARCH: the sample title keyword 'Taming' does not exist in this app's seeded data (0 of 12, correctly showed 'no sessions match' — a data/vocabulary substitution, not a bug); searching speaker surname 'Raman' correctly narrowed to 1 of 12 sessions. Clear-filter chip restored the full list.
- SESSIONS FILTERS: facets are plain Day/Track/Format/Room selects (auto-applying) rather than a slide-out panel; selecting Track='Platform & Infra' narrowed to 5 of 12, all verified to carry that track tag; cleared successfully.
- SPEAKERS LIST: 12 of 12, alphabetical by surname (Brightwell→Zabala) confirmed. Priya Raman's card and detail page audited: headshot, name, title, company, bio (Show more), LinkedIn, and a 'Sessions (1)' list with title/date-time/room. Name search 'Priya Raman' correctly narrowed to 1 of 1.
- AGENDA: hybrid time-gutter + room-column layout (time rows with side-by-side room cards, inline break rows), with a 'Rooms in use today' sidebar and printable one-pager. Verified day-switch (Wed 12 → Thu 13) showed different sessions. Opened a session detail (full time range, track/format tags, speaker, full description, no subsessions present) and confirmed Back-to-Agenda restores state.
- SPEAKER GALLERY: photo grid at /gallery (List/Grid tabs on the same page family). 3/12 speakers have real headshot images, 9/12 gracefully fall back to two-letter initial placeholders. Gallery cards show name+company but omit job title (present on List view) — minor content-parity gap flagged. Name search and open/close of speaker detail verified with screenshots.
- CONSISTENCY SAMPLING: session 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective' / speaker Priya Raman shown identically (title, date, time, room, track) across Sessions list, Agenda, Agenda detail, and Speaker detail — no mismatches found.
- BUG: Priya Raman's public bio contains a leaked test-fixture marker string 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01' embedded mid-sentence, visible on both /speakers and /gallery detail pages — evidence of test data contamination reaching the public surface.
- Per-surface access record: all five surfaces (Sessions, Speakers List, Agenda, Speaker Gallery, Embeds) rendered as fully anonymous public pages; none ever required attendee login or organizer/admin privileges to read.

All required screenshots were captured (sessions list, show-more before/after, search narrowing x2, track filter before/after, speakers list, speaker detail, speaker search, agenda day1, agenda day2, agenda session detail, gallery grid, gallery search, gallery speaker detail, embed surface).
observations: Homepage (http://localhost:8890/) is anonymous, lists one event 'DevFlow Conf 2027' with no login required, links to public event site /e/devflow-conf-2027/sessions and /submit/devflow-conf-2027. No admin credentials were used. The public Sessions page at /e/devflow-conf-2027/sessions is fully readable with NO login at all — no auth wall encountered. Content is NOT limited to a single approved session; 12 sessions are visible across Wed(6)/Thu(4)/Fri(2), so the content-approval gate mentioned in the precondition does not appear to be restricting output in this run (or all scheduled sessions are already approved). Proceeding with the tour without needing organizer login.

SESSIONS LIST field audit (3 cards): (1) 'Building Resilient Incident Response Pipelines' — title yes, truncated description w/ Show more yes, date+time via day heading 'Wednesday 12 May' + '9:30' yes, room 'Room 2A' yes, speaker name+title+company 'Elliot Ekström · Software Engineer, Eastbrook Digital' yes, Format tag 'Panel, 45 min' yes, Track tag 'Platform & Infra' yes. (2) 'The Hidden Costs of API Design' — same fields present, TWO co-speakers each with name/title/company, room 'Room 2B', 9:30, Track 'Developer Experience', Format 'Keynote, 45 min'. (3) 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective' — Priya Raman, Principal Engineer, Latticework Systems; Thu 13 May 9:30; Room 'Main Stage'; Track 'Platform & Infra'; Format 'Talk, 30 min'. All fields from the checklist present on every card. One card ('Developer Metrics at Scale') showed room as 'To be announced' instead of a room name — graceful handling of unset room.
SEARCH: distinctive title word 'Taming' from the sample script's fixture session does not exist in this app's seeded data (the actual seeded equivalent is 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective') — search correctly returned '0 of 12 sessions, No sessions match your search' (no false positives). Searching speaker surname 'Raman' correctly narrowed to '1 of 12 sessions' showing exactly Priya Raman's talk. Search-clear via the 'Clear' chip works and restores all 12.
FILTER: Filters are plain <select> comboboxes inline in the toolbar (Days/Tracks/Formats/Rooms), not a separate slide-out panel — facet groups are: All days, All tracks (AI Engineering / Platform & Infra / Developer Experience / Community), All formats (Keynote/Talk/Lightning Talk/Workshop/Panel), All rooms (Main Stage/Room 2A/Room 2B/Workshop Lab/Overflow Room). Selecting 'Platform & Infra' auto-applied (no separate Apply click needed) and narrowed to 5 of 12 sessions; all 5 visible cards carried the 'PLATFORM & INFRA' track label. Filter cleared via 'Clear' chip restored all 12.

AGENDA structure: it is a hybrid time-ordered/grid layout — each day page groups sessions into time-slot rows (a time gutter, e.g. '9:30', '11:00', '13:00', '14:00') and within a row, concurrent sessions are laid out side-by-side in room-labeled cards (e.g. Room 2A / Room 2B at 9:30). Breaks (coffee, lunch) are shown as their own inline rows. A sidebar lists 'Rooms in use today' with per-room session counts and deep-link anchors. Day navigation is via tabs (Wed 12 / Thu 13 / Fri 14) confirmed working — Wed 12 shows 'Building Resilient Incident Response Pipelines' (Elliot Ekström, Room 2A 9:30) while Thu 13 shows a different set including 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective' (Priya Raman, Main Stage 9:30). Clicking a session block opens a detail view (not a modal — full navigation) showing: Track+Format tag pills, full title, Save toggle, full 'Weekday DD Month, HH:MM-HH:MM · Room' range, speaker link(s), full untruncated description, and a personal-schedule footer. No 'Subsessions' section was present on the sample detail (session had none). 'Back to Agenda' link correctly restores the agenda list at the same day.

SPEAKER GALLERY (photo grid) at /e/devflow-conf-2027/gallery, toggled via List/Grid tab shared with the Speakers list page (same route family, different view param). 12 of 12 speakers shown. Cards show: photo/placeholder, name, COMPANY ONLY (job title is NOT shown on gallery cards, unlike the List view which shows 'Title, Company') — a minor content-parity gap between List and Grid views. Of 12 speakers, 3 have distinct (blue) headshot images (Toni Brightwell, Alex Delgado, Priya Raman) and 9 degrade gracefully to a two-letter initials placeholder on a diagonal-hatch background (Xan Chen 'XC', Elliot Ekström 'EE', Uma Ionescu 'UI', Frankie Lindqvist 'FL', Val Pereira 'VP', Gale Sandoval 'GS', Wren Whitcombe 'WW', Devon Yilmaz 'DY', Harper Zabala 'HZ') — layout does not break for missing photos. Name search 'Priya Raman' correctly narrowed to 1 of 1 speaker. Clicking a card opens the SAME speaker detail template as the List view (photo, name, title+company, bio with Show more, LinkedIn, 'Sessions (N)' list with title/date-time/room), with a 'Back to Gallery' link that correctly restores the full grid.

BUG FOUND: Priya Raman's bio (visible on both /speakers and /gallery detail views) contains a literal leaked test-fixture marker string 'SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01' concatenated into the middle of the bio paragraph ('...CI reliability, and developer productivity metrics. SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 Priya leads the developer-productivity group at Latticework Systems.'). This looks like an artifact of another automated test (likely a speaker-portal bio-edit scenario) that wrote a tagged sentence into the live/production bio without cleanup, and it renders as-is on the public gallery/speakers pages.

CONSISTENCY SAMPLING — Session 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective' (seed_submission_0001), speaker Priya Raman:
- Sessions list page: Thu 13 May (day heading) · 9:30 · Room 'Main Stage' · speaker 'Priya Raman · Principal Engineer, Latticework Systems' · Track 'Platform & Infra' · Format 'Talk, 30 min'.
- Agenda (Thu 13 tab): 9:30 · Main Stage · same speaker line · same track/format tags — matches exactly.
- Agenda session detail: 'Thursday 13 May, 9:30-10:00 · Main Stage' (adds explicit end time 10:00) · Track/Format tags identical · speaker linked.
- Speaker detail (Priya Raman, from both List and Gallery): Sessions(1) list shows 'Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective — Thursday 13 May, 9:30-10:00 (Main Stage)' — identical day/time/room to the other two surfaces.
No mismatches found across the three surfaces for this session/speaker pair — title, date, time, room, and track were identical everywhere.
Speaker cross-check: Priya Raman appears in both List and Gallery speaker views with identical name/title/company ('Priya Raman', 'Principal Engineer', 'Latticework Systems') in both — except Gallery CARD (not detail) omits the job title, showing only company, while List card shows both — noted above as a minor gap.

FINAL PER-SURFACE SUMMARY (attendee/anonymous tour, no organizer/admin login used except as noted):
1. SESSIONS LIST — Found at /e/devflow-conf-2027/sessions (also mirrored chrome-less at /embed/devflow-conf-2027/sessions with a `fields=` query param controlling which attributes render). Anonymous public page — zero login required at any point; verified by loading directly in a fresh/logged-out browser context. Never required organizer/admin privileges to view.
2. SPEAKERS LIST — Found at /e/devflow-conf-2027/speakers (List view). Anonymous public page, same nav bar as Sessions. No login required.
3. AGENDA — Found at /e/devflow-conf-2027/agenda (with ?day=YYYY-MM-DD for day switching, plus a 'Printable programme' one-pager at /e/devflow-conf-2027/programme). Anonymous public page. No login required.
4. SPEAKER GALLERY (photo grid) — Found at /e/devflow-conf-2027/gallery, exposed as a 'Grid' tab alongside the Speakers List's 'List' tab (shared page family, distinct route). Anonymous public page. No login required.
5. EMBEDS — Found at /embed/devflow-conf-2027/<surface> (confirmed for 'sessions'); renders the same content without the site header/banner chrome, suitable for iframing, with a `fields` param to select which columns/attributes show per session link. Anonymous, no login required.
No surface in this tour ever demanded attendee sign-up or login — the app's whole public program site (sessions, speakers list, agenda, gallery, embeds) is openly readable by an anonymous visitor. The only place credentials were used at all was implicitly not needed: the step-2 admin-approval precondition was NOT invoked because the seeded event already exposed 12 sessions / 12 speakers across all three days without any approval gate blocking content — so no organizer login was performed anywhere in this scenario, consistent with the rule to stay non-admin throughout.
A lightweight 'My schedule' link/localStorage-based save-session feature was also visible in the nav (uses browser storage, 'no account needed', with an ICS calendar download) — an incidental attendee-facing feature beyond the 5 required widgets.
