scenarios.scenarioName: Schedule Itinerary browsing and personal-schedule building
scenarios.summary:
Scenario EMB-S2 fully executed against the DevFlow Conf 2027 public site.

1. ANONYMOUS ACCESS: Navigated logged-out to /e/devflow-conf-2027/{schedule,agenda,sessions}. All itinerary browsing and personal-schedule (Save/Remove) functionality worked with zero authentication - the UI explicitly labels this "no account needed" and stores selections in browser localStorage rather than a server-side user account. No attendee sign-up was ever required or attempted, per the observed behavior (this itself is a finding, not a defect).

2. CHRONOLOGICAL STRUCTURE: Confirmed day tabs (Wed 12 / Thu 13 / Fri 14 May) on both the Agenda and Sessions views, with sessions grouped under ascending time headers (e.g. 9:30, 11:00, 13:00, 14:00) including named breaks (coffee, lunch). Screenshotted Wednesday 12 May's agenda (6 sessions, 4 rooms).

3. SESSION CARD ANATOMY: Selected "Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective" (speaker Priya Raman, Principal Engineer, Latticework Systems) — this is the seeded fixture "Taming 40-Minute CI" under a different title (same abstract text, same speaker). Verified/screenshotted: track chip (Platform & Infra), format+duration (Talk, 30 min), title, speaker name+title+company, full date/time/room (both inline on list and on dedicated detail page), and full description expansion via "Show more"/"Show less" (a <details><summary> control) — expanded and collapsed successfully. No sub-session "View Details" expansion existed beyond this description toggle.

4. DAY SWITCHING: Verified via list/agenda re-render that different days show different session sets (Wed=6, Thu=4, Fri=2 sessions), each screenshotted.

5. SEARCH & FILTER: Keyword search for "Monorepo" narrowed 12→2 sessions with a removable filter chip; cleared successfully. Track filter "Platform & Infra" narrowed 12→5 sessions; cleared successfully. Both screenshotted.

6. PERSONAL SCHEDULE - ADD: Every session card has a "Save"/"Saved" checkbox control. Added two distinct sessions: "Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective" (substituting for "Taming 40-Minute CI") and "From Zero to Test Suites: A Field Guide" (substituting for "Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You," which does not exist in this seed — searching "Lying" returned 0 of 12 results, confirmed and recorded as an explicit substitution). Both shown in "Saved" state via screenshots.

7. MY SCHEDULE VIEW: /e/devflow-conf-2027/schedule showed exactly these 2 sessions, correctly ordered by day/time (Wed 12 14:00 session first, Thu 13 09:30 session second). Screenshotted.

8. PERSISTENCE: Full navigation reload to /schedule after adding sessions still showed "2 saved" with both sessions intact — confirms localStorage-based persistence survives reloads. Screenshotted.

9. EXPORT/CALENDAR: A "Download .ics" link is present in the "Take it with you" panel, generating a URL like /schedule.ics?ids=seed_submission_0010,seed_submission_0001. Clicked once; no in-app confirmation modal appeared (consistent with a direct file-download link), screenshotted before/after.

10. REMOVE: Unchecked the "Remove" control on one saved session; the My Schedule view instantly updated to show exactly 1 remaining session ("Six Minutes, Not Forty..."), with saved-count updating to "1 saved" and the .ics link URL updating accordingly. Screenshotted.

All success signals were captured: two different days of the itinerary, one fully-annotated session card (expanded description), two sessions in added/selected state, personal schedule view with exactly those two sessions in time order, a post-reload persistence screenshot, the export/.ics affordance, and an explicit record that browsing/schedule-building was fully anonymous (no login required at any point).
observations: Navigated anonymously (logged out) to /e/devflow-conf-2027/schedule ("My schedule" page). It loaded without requiring login, showing "0 saved in this browser · no account needed" and a Download .ics option - so personal schedule building appears to work anonymously via browser storage, not requiring an attendee account.

Clicked "Download .ics" link (href: /e/devflow-conf-2027/schedule.ics?ids=seed_submission_0010,seed_submission_0001). This is a direct file-download link (Content-Disposition triggered by browser), not a modal/confirmation - no on-page confirmation text appeared, consistent with a real .ics file download. Did not open the downloaded file per instructions. This satisfies the export/add-to-calendar affordance requirement.

SUMMARY OF FINDINGS for EMB-S2: (1) Itinerary/agenda browsing worked fully anonymously (logged out) at /e/devflow-conf-2027/{sessions,agenda,schedule} - no login was ever required, and the app explicitly states "no account needed" for personal-schedule building (stored in browser localStorage, not server-side account). This is a notable design choice: schedule persistence is per-browser rather than per-account. (2) Day tabs (Wed 12/Thu 13/Fri 14) with sessions grouped chronologically under time headers confirmed on both /agenda and /sessions pages. (3) Session card anatomy verified: track chip, format+duration, title, speaker name+title+company, time/room, and expandable "Show more" full description (via <summary>/<details>). Detail page adds full date/time line and room plus speaker link. (4) Keyword search (e.g. "Monorepo") and track filter (Platform & Infra) both work, narrowing results with a removable filter chip and an easy "Clear". (5) Fixture session "Taming 40-Minute CI" was found renamed as "Six Minutes, Not Forty: A Monorepo CI Caching Retrospective" (same speaker Priya Raman, same abstract text) - clearly the same seed data under a different title. The exact second fixture title "Your AI Pair Programmer Is Lying to You" does NOT exist in this seed (searched "Lying" - 0 of 12 results); substituted "From Zero to Test Suites: A Field Guide" as the second distinct session instead. (6) Personal schedule ("Save"/"Saved" checkbox on every card) successfully added both chosen sessions, confirmed on the /schedule view showing exactly 2 in day/time order. (7) Reload/persistence: navigating fresh to /schedule after the additions still showed "2 saved" with both sessions intact - confirms localStorage-based persistence survives navigation (note: did not test after clearing browser storage, which the UI itself warns would clear the list). (8) Export: "Download .ics" link present and generates a per-selection ICS URL (schedule.ics?ids=...); clicked once, browser-download behavior inferred from direct link href (no separate confirmation modal appeared, consistent with a file download). (9) Remove control: unchecking "Remove" checkbox on a saved session instantly dropped it from My Schedule, leaving exactly 1 session, confirmed via snapshot and screenshot.

scenarios.scenarioName: Organizer embed generation, snippet retrieval and data consistency
scenarios.summary:
Completed all steps of EMB-S3 as organizer (Jordan Alvarez / sbek-organizer@example.com) on the seeded DevFlow Conf 2027 event (app: "Chautauqua").

1. LOGIN: Signed in via /login using the seeded organizer demo-account button; landed on /admin/overview.

2. EVENT WORKSPACE: DevFlow Conf 2027 was pre-seeded and selected by default (top-bar "Switch event" shows it) — no event creation was needed for this scenario.

3. EMBED AREA LOCATION: Found under Admin > Settings > "Public pages" section, sub-region "Saved embeds" (URL /admin/settings?section=public-pages). Screenshotted the landing list (screenshots 007/008/013/014). Existing embeds ARE listed with: a Name, a stable URL (/embed/e/<id>), a type/format grouping line (e.g. "Sessions · iframe · AI Engineering · 6 fields", "Sessions · json · Limit 20 · 4 fields"), and an ON/OFF enabled-state label with a "Turn on/Turn off" button. No search/filter control exists for this short (4-item) list. Separately, each of the 6 core Public Pages (Sessions, Speakers, Agenda, Schedule and ICS, Speaker gallery, CFP submit page) has its own lightweight "Embed code" button.

4. NEW EMBED BUILDER: Clicked "New embed"; captured the type ("Surface") and format pickers (screenshot 009). Surfaces offered: Sessions, Speakers, Agenda, Schedule, Gallery — matching all 5 requested widget types. Formats offered: iframe, element, link, json, xml (no explicit "iCal" in this generic builder, though the Schedule public page exposes a separate .ics feed URL under Settings > Your data).

5. CONFIGURATION: Built a Sessions-list embed named "QA Test Sessions Widget" with Track filter = Platform & Infra, accent color branding (#2255aa), and field-selection toggle chips (Track/Time/Room/Speaker/Format on, Description off). Screenshotted the configured builder (010/011). Other available filters: Session format, Room ID, Day, Search text, numeric Limit. No custom-CSS field was found.

6. SAVE + GET CODE: Saved the embed (appeared in the Saved Embeds list as ON). Recorded the live-preview (unsaved) snippet verbatim and the persistent "Get code" snippet verbatim (both recorded as observations), plus the extracted embed URL: http://localhost:8890/embed/e/kzbabxpphvqtn5ylvvla. Screenshots 015/016.

7. RENDERED CHECK: Navigated directly to the saved embed URL on the same origin. It rendered a fully working, chromeless Sessions widget filtered to Platform & Infra (5/5 sessions), grouped by day, with working search/format/room filters and the configured field set — screenshot 018.

8. TOGGLE STATE: Recorded enable/disable presentation (ON/OFF label + Turn on/Turn off button); did not disable/delete any embed I didn't create, and did not modify existing seeded embeds' state.

9/10. CONSISTENCY CHECK: Recorded organizer-side session SES-011 "Observability Anti-Patterns We Finally Fixed" (Track: Platform & Infra, Format: Lightning Talk 10 min, Wed 12 May 14:00–14:45, Room 2A, Speaker: Harper Zabala) via /admin/submissions/seed_submission_0011 (screenshot 022). Opened the same session on the public attendee-facing surface /e/devflow-conf-2027/sessions/seed_submission_0011 (screenshot 024) — every field (title, track, format, date/time, room, speaker, abstract) matched exactly with no discrepancies.

All success signals were satisfied: embed list + picker screenshots, verbatim snippet with extracted URL, a genuine rendered-embed screenshot (not deferred), and a matching organizer/public screenshot pair.
observations: Embeds area found at Admin > Settings > Public pages, section "Saved embeds". Existing embeds ARE listed with: name (e.g. "AI track sessions"), a direct URL (/embed/e/seed_embed_NNNN), a type/format grouping line (e.g. "Sessions · iframe · AI Engineering · 6 fields", "Sessions · json · Limit 20 · 4 fields"), and an enabled/disabled state shown as ON/OFF text plus a Turn on/Turn off button. No search or filter control is present in this list (only 4 items, static list, no search box). Additionally, above Saved Embeds, each of the 6 core Public Pages (Sessions, Speakers, Agenda, Schedule and ICS, Speaker gallery, CFP submit page) has its own quick "Embed code" button — a lighter-weight embed-code affordance separate from the named/saved embed builder.

Embed builder widget types offered as "Surface": Sessions, Speakers, Agenda, Schedule, Gallery — exactly the 5 equivalents requested (sessions list, speakers list, agenda, schedule itinerary, speaker gallery). Output "Format" options offered: iframe, element, link, json, xml (no explicit "iCal" format in this generic builder, though the Schedule public page separately exposes a .ics URL at /e/devflow-conf-2027/agenda.ics per Settings > Your data). Configuration options available: Track filter (dropdown: all tracks/AI Engineering/Platform & Infra/Developer Experience/Community), Session format filter (free text), Room ID filter, Day filter, Search filter, Limit (numeric), Fields shown (toggle chips: Track, Time, Room, Speaker, Description, Format), and Accent color (branding). No custom CSS field was found.

VERBATIM generated snippet (iframe format, Sessions surface, track=Platform & Infra, accent=#2255aa, fields=track,time,room,speaker,format i.e. Description unchecked): <iframe src="http://localhost:8890/embed/devflow-conf-2027/sessions?trackId=seed_track_0002&fields=track%2Ctime%2Croom%2Cspeaker%2Cformat&accent=2255aa" style="width:100%;min-height:600px;border:0" loading="lazy" title="sessions"></iframe>
Embedded URL extracted from the snippet (iframe src / feed endpoint): http://localhost:8890/embed/devflow-conf-2027/sessions?trackId=seed_track_0002&fields=track%2Ctime%2Croom%2Cspeaker%2Cformat&accent=2255aa

After clicking "Save embed" the item appeared in the Saved Embeds list as: "QA Test Sessions Widget /embed/e/kzbabxpphvqtn5ylvvla Sessions · iframe · Platform & Infra · 5 fields ON". Clicking its "Get code" button revealed a STABLE persistent snippet (verbatim): <iframe src="http://localhost:8890/embed/e/kzbabxpphvqtn5ylvvla" style="width:100%;min-height:600px;border:0" loading="lazy" title="sessions"></iframe>
This differs from the live/unsaved builder snippet (which encoded filters directly in query params on /embed/devflow-conf-2027/sessions) — the saved version uses a short stable ID URL (/embed/e/<id>) that the app says "carries the embed's name, so changing these settings updates every page it is pasted on" (i.e. edits propagate without needing to update the pasted snippet). Persistent embed URL: http://localhost:8890/embed/e/kzbabxpphvqtn5ylvvla

Rendered check: navigated directly to the saved embed's persistent URL (http://localhost:8890/embed/e/kzbabxpphvqtn5ylvvla) on the same origin. It rendered a fully functional, chromeless Sessions list widget correctly filtered to "Platform & Infra" track (5 of 5 sessions matching), with working search box and format/room filter dropdowns, grouped by day (Wednesday 12 May, Thursday 13 May), showing session time, room, title (linked), speaker name+title+company, track badge, and format badge — consistent with the "fields shown" configuration selected in the builder (track, time, room, speaker, format enabled; description disabled).

Enable/disable toggle for saved embeds: presented as a plain-text state label ("ON" / "OFF") next to each row, paired with a button that reads "Turn off" (if currently on) or "Turn on" (if currently off). Current states observed: AI track sessions=ON, Last year's speakers=OFF, Homepage agenda strip=ON, Sponsor deck feed=OFF, QA Test Sessions Widget (newly created)=ON by default. Did not toggle any existing embed's state, per instructions.

Organizer-side session record captured for consistency check: Title="Observability Anti-Patterns We Finally Fixed", Record ID=SES-011, Track="Platform & Infra", Format="Lightning Talk (10 min)", Date/Time="Wed 12 May · 14:00–14:45", Room="Room 2A", Speaker="Harper Zabala (Harborline Cloud · Software Engineer)". Decision: Accepted.

CONSISTENCY CHECK PASSED: Public attendee-facing surface (http://localhost:8890/e/devflow-conf-2027/sessions/seed_submission_0011, no login required) displays session SES-011 as: Title="Observability Anti-Patterns We Finally Fixed" (exact match), Track="Platform & Infra" (exact match), Format="Lightning Talk, 10 min" (exact match), Date/Time="Wednesday 12 May, 14:00-14:45" (exact match), Room="Room 2A" (exact match), Speaker="Harper Zabala" (exact match, linked to full speaker profile). Abstract text also matches verbatim. No discrepancies found between organizer admin record and public/attendee-facing rendering.

areas.title: Speaker CRM (Cross-Event Speaker Database)

items.reasoning: A 'Contacts' area exists in the admin top nav as a peer of event modules and is explicitly org-scoped: contact drawers separate the 'org-wide record' from per-event facts and include an 'ACROSS YOUR EVENTS' history. The directory renders a table with name+email (plus company/title/labels) for 40 people; typing 'Priya' narrowed it to the 2 matching rows ('Showing 1–2 of 2') and clearing the box restored the full 40-person list.
evidence_refs: obs: Found a 'Contacts' nav item in the admin SPA ... Directory / Duplicates / Segments / Pipeline tabs

items.reasoning: A rule-based filter builder ('Matching all of' + Add a rule) exists beyond text search. Company contains 'Labs' narrowed to '6 of 40 match' with only Labs companies listed; adding a second rule (Title contains 'Staff') narrowed further to '2 of 40 match' (AND behaviour). Each rule has a Remove control, and a later unfiltered directory view again shows all 40 people, confirming filters are clearable.

The profile drawer shows full identity data (first/last name, email, phone, company, title, bio, links) plus a strong cross-event history surface: an 'ACROSS YOUR EVENTS' section listing linked sessions per event with statuses and timestamped communication/activity entries. A Notes field exists and was filled; the final-state screenshot shows the note rendered as a saved-looking read-only value. However, the drawer warns 'nothing is saved until you press Save' and no post-reload screenshot of the note was captured, so note persistence is not proven.

Organizer-defined metadata UI clearly exists: an 'Add field' control on the contact drawer produced a custom 'Speaker Type' = 'External' row (with Remove), and the app also carries labels/tags (ROLE SPEAKER, YEAR 2027) that surface as a directory LABELS column. But the custom field was captured only in edit state and no save-confirmation or post-reload screenshot exists, so persistence of the organizer-created field/value is unverified.

A four-step Import CSV wizard (Choose file → Match columns → Review → Done) accepted the speakers.csv fixture (3 rows), auto-mapped columns, flagged an email-match row as 'Update' and a fuzzy name/company match as a possible duplicate with import-as-new vs merge choice, then completed with 'Created 2, updated 1, skipped 0.' The header count rose 38 → 40 people and imported rows appear in the directory (e.g. Priya Raman / priya.speaker@sbek-test.example.com, Dana Kowalski / dana.speaker@sbek-test.example.com).

Duplicate surfacing is clearly implemented: a header counter ('5 possible duplicates'), a Duplicates tab listing pairs with match reasons ('Same name and company', 'Same email', 'Same name, different company') and per-pair 'Merge' / 'Keep both' actions, plus in-review duplicate detection during CSV import with a merge-into-existing option. However the evidence never shows a merge being executed: no comparison/primary-selection step, and the directory still shows 40 people / 5 duplicates afterwards, so the post-merge single-surviving-record requirement is unverified.

The Pipeline tab shows a kanban with five named stages including terminal ones: Identified, Contacted, Interested, Confirmed, Declined (20 people, 'drag between columns'). 'Add to the pipeline' enrolled directory contact Marcus Okafor (contact search, starting stage, Fit 1–5, 'Why them' rationale); the board then showed him in Identified (21 people, Identified 5). Via the card's Stage selector he was moved Identified → Contacted → Interested; the board before reload and the after-reload screenshot both show the card in Interested with Interested count 5, confirming persistence.

The pipeline card detail exposes Stage, Fit/rationale, an 'Add a note' composer with Save note, and an ACTIVITY log. After saving, the log shows the note ('Note: Left voicemail 2027-01-15; follow up next week. — Jordan Alvarez, 16 Aug, 21:40') plus timestamped stage transitions 'Moved Contacted → Interested', 'Moved Identified → Contacted', 'Moved Enrolled → Identified' (all 16 Aug, 21:39), matching the moves performed. The after-reload card-detail screenshot shows the same saved note and transition history, confirming persistence.

With two filter rules active a 'Save as a segment' action appears; the Segments tab offers a name field showing the rules ('company contains "Labs" AND title contains "Staff"'). Saving 'AI Experts' incremented Segments · 1 → 2 and the segment appears in the SAVED SEGMENTS panel with a member count of 2 and its rule text. Selecting Segment: 'AI Experts' in the directory dropdown reopens it showing the 2 matching contacts ('Showing 1–2 of 2'). No dynamic/curated type choice offered (bonus only).

The contact drawer offers 'Add to event', opening an 'Add to an event' dialog with an event picker, role choice (Speaker/Co-presenter/Moderator/Panelist) and session title; it also reports existing participation ('Marcus Okafor is already on this event — 1 session' for DevFlow Conf 2027). Because Marcus was already on 2027, the agent targeted a second event (DevFlow Conf 2028) — the push succeeded with an in-app confirmation ('Marcus Okafor was added as an accepted speaker. View in Speakers') and he then appears in that event's Speakers module with name and company (Cloudreach Labs) and generated speaker tasks, i.e. no re-entry. Gap: the event speakers table shows name/company but not email, and the target event was 2028 rather than 2027, though the picker demonstrably lists 2027 too.

There are hints that bulk email exists — row checkboxes with the hint 'Tick rows to email contacts in bulk' and an 'Email' button on the contact drawer — but both scenarios hit the turn limit before a composer was opened. No evidence of a composer, subject/body entry, merge-tag preview, send confirmation or sent-history log was captured, so the UI-observable half cannot be assessed.

The CRM landing view carries org-wide KPI counters in its header — '40 people · 29 speakers · 5 possible duplicates' — consistent with the 40-row directory (and consistent with the pre-import 38 → post-import 40 change). A populated analytics widget renders in the right rail: 'WHERE THEY WORK' top-companies breakdown (Bluepeak Labs 4, Cartwheel Software 4, Fernway Technologies 4, Driftline 3, Eastbrook Digital 3), alongside saved-segment counts and duplicate pairs. Gaps: it is the directory landing rather than a dedicated dashboard, and no widget click-through drill-down was demonstrated.

defects.description: In the CSV import review step, rows flagged as 'Possible duplicate' default to 'Import as new', so an untouched import silently creates new duplicate records (possible-duplicate count rose 4 → 5 and two identical 'Priya Raman' rows now exist in the directory). Safer default or forced choice would prevent duplicate proliferation.
defects.where: Contacts → Import CSV → Review step; directory duplicate counter

defects.description: The contact drawer mixes staged edits with read-only display: it warns 'Click a row to edit — nothing is saved until you press Save', yet edited values (notes, newly added custom field) render like persisted values once focus moves, making it ambiguous whether data has actually been committed.
defects.where: Contacts → contact drawer (Notes / Add field sections)

defects.description: Skeleton placeholder rows are shown for the Contacts and event Speakers pages with no content or spinner labelling, so navigations can appear stuck mid-load.

areas.notes: Both scenarios ended at the 70-turn limit (harness limitation, not an app fault), which left three areas unverified: bulk email composition/send (CRM-11 never reached), execution of a merge from the Duplicates tab (CRM-06), and reload-based persistence checks for the contact note and custom field (CRM-03/CRM-04). Everything the agent did reach worked smoothly: the Contacts module is a genuinely cross-event CRM (org-wide record vs per-event facts, 'Across your events' session history), with rule-based filtering, saved segments, a 5-stage kanban with a timestamped activity log, a full CSV import wizard with dedupe review, and a working push-to-event flow that generated speaker tasks in the target event. Note that CRM-10 was demonstrated against a newly created 'DevFlow Conf 2028' because the chosen contact was already on DevFlow Conf 2027; the picker did list 2027, so the capability is the same.

scenarios.scenarioName: Build and organize the speaker database
scenarios.summary: Turn limit (70) reached before the scenario finished.
observations: Found a 'Contacts' nav item in the admin SPA (alongside Overview/Submissions/Review/Speakers/Content/Agenda/Comms/Settings) that acts as a CRM: it shows 38 people / 29 speakers / 4 possible duplicates, with Directory / Duplicates / Segments / Pipeline tabs, a rule-based filter builder ('Matching all of' + Add a rule), saved segments panel, and per-row 'Merge' suggestions for likely duplicates. This appears to be the cross-event speaker CRM equivalent (distinct from the per-event 'Speakers' roster tab). Need to confirm whether contacts persist across multiple events by creating a second event later.

CRM-06 evidence: Import wizard detects duplicates during Review step (email match => 'Update', name+company fuzzy match => flagged as 'Possible duplicate' with radio choice 'Import as new' vs 'Merge into existing contact'). We chose 'Import as new' for Priya Raman (matched against seeded speaker record with different email) to test behavior - this created a NEW duplicate contact rather than silently deduping automatically. Duplicate count rose from 4 to 5 after import, confirming the import does NOT auto-merge by default; it leaves the decision to the operator during review, and untouched choices default to 'Import as new'. Directory now shows 40 people / 29 speakers / 5 possible duplicates after importing the 3-row speakers.csv (2 created: new Priya Raman variant + Dana Kowalski; 1 updated: Marcus Okafor's existing seeded contact by email match).

areas.title: Speaker Management

items.reasoning: A dedicated /admin/speakers roster renders every speaker with name plus company (Toni Brightwell · Junction Point, Xan Chen · Driftline, etc.) and participation badges. Typing "Priya" into the search box narrows the list to a single row with the explicit caption "Showing 1 of 15 speakers · matching 'Priya' and participation confirmed", and later unfiltered captures show the full roster restored after the query was cleared (transcript turns 9–12 fill and then clear the search; turn 28 reload shows the full list again).

The "Add speaker" dialog accepts first/last name, email, title, company and a full bio (all visibly filled), i.e. more than the required name/email/bio. The organizer-side record for Priya displays name, company · title, bio and email. The organizer bio edit with sentinel SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01 was entered in the contact record and, after navigating back to the speaker record page, the bio renders "...productivity metrics. SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01", so the edit persisted across a page load. Gap: no explicit creation-success state was captured for the manual add (the dialog flagged a possible duplicate and the run ended before an unambiguous 'added' confirmation), so persistence of a brand-new record is inferred rather than directly shown.

An import path clearly exists in the UI: the Add-speaker dialog contains a link "Import speakers from a CSV" (/admin/contacts?import=1&eventId=...) and the Contacts page shows an "Import CSV" button. However the SPK-S1 run reached its turn limit before the speakers.csv fixture was ever uploaded, and no roster screenshot shows Dana Kowalski. The capability was therefore never exercised — insufficient evidence to score the import outcome.

Priya's record initially showed a "MIXED · SES-001 confirmed · SES-031 not invited" participation state with a CONFIRMED▾ status dropdown; the agent used the roster status control (turns 31–32) and subsequent record views loaded from fresh navigations consistently show a single CONFIRMED badge, i.e. the change persisted. The roster also carries an "Any participation" filter which, set to Confirmed, produced "Showing 1 of 15 speakers · matching 'Priya' and participation confirmed", demonstrating correct status filtering.

The New-task dialog accepts a title ("Confirm participation"), instructions, a due date (April 1, 2027), a kind (Upload/Form/Acknowledge), a Required flag and multi-select assignment — Marcus Okafor and Priya Raman both checked under "Only the people I choose". A "Task created." toast is visible, and the organizer task matrix afterwards gained columns "Complete bio and profile · DUE 1 APR 2027 · REQUIRED" and "Confirm participation · DUE 1 APR 2027 · REQUIRED" with "—" for unassigned speakers, showing due dates and assignee scoping at list level. Only two of the three fixture tasks were created because the run hit its turn limit, but the creation/assignment capability itself is fully demonstrated.

Explicit per-speaker controls exist on the speaker record ("Email Priya", "Remind Priya") and bulk controls on the roster ("Remind all outstanding", per-row "Remind …"). A bulk send using the pre-built "Speaker Portal Invitation" template reported "SEND COMPLETE — 29 of 33 speakers were emailed" and was recorded in the Comms history (16 Aug 21:02, template Speaker Portal Invitation, 29 sent · 4 skipped) with per-recipient SENT rows.
evidence_refs: obs: Comms history log confirms the bulk send

items.reasoning: Password sign-in as sbek-speaker@example.com landed on /portal, a distinct speaker-facing UI headed "5 things to do" with "PRIYA RAMAN" in the header and footer "Priya Raman · Latticework Systems", listing only her tasks, submissions, session and profile. The agent explicitly re-checked scoping across dashboard, submissions, session detail, profile and tasks and found no Marcus/Dana data — Marcus appears only as legitimate co-presenter on Priya's own shared session.
evidence_refs: obs: Portal dashboard identifies speaker as "Priya Raman"

items.reasoning: The portal profile form edits bio, Twitter, LinkedIn, GitHub, website and headshot. After save the page shows "Profile saved." / "Headshot uploaded." with the sentinel bio SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01 in the field and an avatar image rendered; a fresh reload of /portal/profile shows the same sentinel and avatar. Organizer-side, Priya's speaker record renders the identical bio ending "...productivity metrics. SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01" plus a headshot image with a Download link, so the portal edit propagated without re-entry. Caveat: the rendered avatar looks identical (solid blue circle) before and after upload, so the image swap itself is not visually verifiable — the upload confirmation and persistence are the supporting evidence.

Priya's /portal/tasks lists every assigned task with a due date and a TO DO / DONE state, including the two organizer-created general tasks "Confirm participation" (Due Thu 1 Apr 2027) and "Complete bio and profile" (Due Thu 1 Apr 2027), both initially TO DO with a "Mark complete" button. Clicking each flipped it to DONE, and the reloaded list shows both DONE while "Announce participation" and "Hotel stay requirement form" remain TO DO with their due dates — persistent mixed completion. Only two fixture tasks existed because the organizer scenario timed out before creating the release-form task; that is a run artifact, not a missing capability.
evidence_refs: obs: Task list for Priya shows 8 tasks total

items.reasoning: The headshot is visible organizer-side on Priya's record with a working "Download" control that responded without error, and a separate Files table on the record lists a task attachment (onboarding-deliverable.pdf, 430 B) with a download link. However, the headshot entry shows no filename, uploader or timestamp metadata — the agent explicitly recorded that only a bare Download link exists — so the metadata half of the criterion is unmet.
evidence_refs: obs: Priya's headshot is displayed as an image at the top of her organizer record with only a bare "Download" link

items.reasoning: Priya's organizer record shows a SESSIONS · 2 block including "SES-031 · Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale — Wed 12 May 15:00–15:30, Room 2A" with an ACCEPTED status. In the portal, the same session appears under her submissions/"Your session" with title, format, track, room and time and co-presenter Marcus Okafor (turns 9–13, session detail page /portal/submissions/...).

The Speakers roster is itself a progress matrix: speakers as rows, tasks as columns with due dates, and COMPLETE / PENDING / OVERDUE badges per cell — no record needs to be opened. Filtering to "Priya" showed her Confirm participation and Complete bio and profile as Complete (post-portal completions), while "Marcus" showed both as PENDING, giving the required mixed state across two speakers. The "Any task status" filter was exercised with Pending and Complete values and narrowed the list correctly (14 of 15 vs 15 of 15). The release-form task could not be checked because it was never created.

The Comms compose wizard has four steps (Recipients → Template → Preview → Send). Recipients are chosen from filterable speaker/submission lists with checkboxes (32 selected, filters Pending/Accepted/Declined etc.). The compose step carries the fixture subject "Welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027 speakers" plus a body; the send step reported "SEND COMPLETE — 29 of 33 speakers were emailed" with a skipped list and reasons; the History tab logs the send at 16 Aug 21:02 with subject, template and "29 sent · 4 skipped", expandable to per-recipient SENT rows with "Show what was sent".

The compose flow uses a saved template ("Speaker Portal Invitation", one of several listed in History filters) whose body contains merge tokens {speaker_name}, {event_name}, {portal_link}, with an "Insert a field" picker (7 fields) and the note "Merge fields fill in per recipient — shown resolved in Preview". The per-recipient preview renders "Hi Priya Raman, welcome to DevFlow Conf 2027! ... your speaker portal: http://localhost:8799/portal", demonstrably resolving tokens to real data.

The contact detail dialog exposes Dietary / Travel / Accessibility logistics fields; the agent set Dietary = "Vegetarian" and Travel = "Arrival May 11, aisle seat; dietary: Vegetarian" and saved. Priya's speaker record then shows a "LOGISTICS · ORG-WIDE" panel with Dietary: Vegetarian and Travel: Arrival May 11, aisle seat…, and the same values are still present on a subsequently reloaded record view.

defects.description: Merge-field {portal_link} resolves to http://localhost:8799/portal in the rendered email preview, while the application is served on port 8890 — recipients would receive a portal link pointing at the wrong host/port.

Duplicate speaker/contact records exist for the same email: the bulk send skipped three separate "Priya Raman" rows all with sbek-speaker@example.com ("Same message, same address, already in this batch") and Contacts flags "4 possible duplicates" including "Marcus Okafor · Marcus Okafor". The Add-speaker dialog warns "Possible duplicate" but does not prevent creating another record.
defects.where: Comms send-complete skipped list and Contacts directory (SPK-S3/screenshots/023-comms-send-success.jpg, SPK-S1/screenshots/016-auto-admin-contacts.jpg, SPK-S1/screenshots/009-add-speaker-duplicate-detected.jpg)

defects.description: The speaker-uploaded headshot is shown organizer-side only as an image with a bare "Download" link — no filename, uploader or upload timestamp — and it is not listed in the record's Files table alongside other uploads, making provenance untraceable.
defects.where: Admin → Speakers → Priya Raman record (obs in SPK-S3; SPK-S3/screenshots/016-auto-admin-speakers-seed-contact-0001.jpg)

areas.notes: Two of three scenarios (SPK-S1, SPK-S3) ended on the 70-turn limit rather than completing, which is an evaluation-run limitation, not an app fault. Consequences for grading: the speakers.csv import was never attempted (SPK-03 → cannot_judge despite visible "Import CSV" / "Import speakers from a CSV" controls), and only two of the three fixture general tasks were created, so SPK-05/09/12 were judged on the demonstrated capability with the missing third task noted. Several auto-captured screenshots show loading skeletons, indicating the admin pages render placeholders briefly on navigation; this was not treated as a defect. Overall the clone ("Chautauqua") implements a rich speaker-management surface: roster matrix with search/status/task filters, per-speaker records with sessions, tasks, logistics and headshot, a scoped speaker portal with profile editing and task completion, and a four-step comms wizard with templates, merge fields, previews and a full send history.

scenarios.scenarioName: Speaker completes onboarding in the portal
scenarios.summary:
Completed SPK-S2 speaker portal onboarding scenario against the Chautauqua app.

1. Signed in at /login as Priya Raman (sbek-speaker@example.com) - account pre-existed (seeded), landed on /portal.
2. Dashboard clearly identifies "Priya Raman" (top nav + footer "Priya Raman · Latticework Systems") and is a distinct speaker-facing UI (heading "5 things to do", "Your submissions", "Your session", "Done" sections) - not the organizer admin.
3. Scoping verified: no data belonging to Marcus Okafor (other than his name as a legitimate co-presenter on Priya's own shared session "Taming 40-Minute CI") or Dana Kowalski appeared anywhere on the dashboard, submissions, session-detail, profile, or tasks pages.
4. Found and confirmed the target session "Taming 40-Minute CI: Incremental Builds at Monorepo Scale" (SES-031, Talk 30 min, Platform & Infra, Accepted) with room/time "Wed 12 May, 15:00 · Room 2A" and co-presenter Marcus Okafor shown.
5. Edited profile at /portal/profile: updated bio to include sentinel "SBEK-PORTAL-BIO-01" (appended to existing bio, which already carried an earlier "SBEK-ORG-EDIT-01" sentinel from a prior scenario, confirming continuity), verified Twitter (@priyabuilds) and LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/priya-raman-example) fields were pre-filled/fixture-matching, and uploaded fixtures/headshot.png. Screenshotted filled form pre-save, then saved - got "Profile saved."/"Headshot uploaded." confirmations, headshot rendered as an avatar image (solid color, consistent with the fixture file).
6. Reloaded /portal/profile - bio sentinel and headshot both persisted identically.
7. Opened /portal/tasks - found 8 seeded tasks (not exactly the 3 named in the script). Recorded an explicit observation that no task literally named "Sign speaker release form" exists in this seed data; closest equivalents (Hotel stay requirement form, Finalize bio+headshot, Announce participation) exist instead. This is a data/vocabulary mismatch, not a missing capability - the task system fully supports required flags, due dates, mark-complete buttons, and even file-upload tasks with version history and commenting.
8. Marked "Confirm participation" complete via its "Mark complete" button - status flipped To do → Done immediately (screenshotted before/after).
9. Marked "Complete bio and profile" complete the same way - status flipped To do → Done (screenshotted).
10. Left "Announce participation" (and "Hotel stay requirement form") incomplete as substitutes for the absent "Sign speaker release form" task, to preserve the mixed-completion state requested by the script.
11. Reloaded /portal/tasks - confirmed both completed tasks persisted as Done with their due dates, while the substitute incomplete tasks remained To do with their due dates, producing the mixed-completion final state.

All success signals were verified: portal identifies Priya with proper scoping, her session title/room/time visible, sentinel bio + headshot render and persist, and the task list shows due dates with 2 completed / remaining incomplete tasks persisting after reload (using the app's own task vocabulary since an exact "Sign speaker release form" task does not exist in this seed data).
observations: Portal dashboard identifies speaker as "Priya Raman" in top-right nav and footer ("Priya Raman · Latticework Systems"). Dashboard heading "5 things to do" and all listed items (tasks, submissions, sessions) reference only Priya's own data. No mention of Marcus Okafor or Dana Kowalski anywhere on the dashboard page - confirming per-speaker scoping. Note: task list shows 5 tasks (not the 3 named in the scenario script) - likely additional seed tasks from prior scenario runs (Hotel stay requirement form, Finalize bio+headshot, Announce participation) alongside the expected Confirm participation / Complete bio and profile / Sign speaker release form. Will locate the exact 3 tasks named in script on the task list page.

Headshot renders as a solid blue circle both immediately after upload and after a full page reload — consistent behavior suggests the headshot.png fixture is itself a solid-color test image (this is the actual uploaded image rendering, not a placeholder, since it persisted identically across reload with 'No file chosen' shown in the file input, confirming the stored image is being displayed).

Task list for Priya shows 8 tasks total (not the 3 named in the SPK-S2 script): Hotel stay requirement form (To do, required, form-fill type), Flight reimbursement form (Done), Finalize talk description (Done), Finalize bio + headshot (Done), Announce participation (To do), Upload your slide deck (Done, with file/version history/comments), Confirm participation (To do, required), Complete bio and profile (To do, required). There is NO task literally named "Sign speaker release form" in this seed data — closest equivalents already exist and are marked Done (Finalize bio+headshot) or To do (Hotel stay requirement form, Announce participation). This is a data/vocabulary mismatch, not a missing capability: the portal clearly supports required tasks, due dates, mark-complete buttons, and file-upload tasks with versioning/comments. Per script step 10, I will leave "Announce participation" (an existing To-do task with no release-form equivalent) incomplete to demonstrate mixed completion, after completing "Confirm participation" and "Complete bio and profile" as instructed.

Final scoping re-check: throughout the entire portal session (dashboard, submissions, session detail, profile, tasks pages) the only other speaker name encountered was "Marcus Okafor" listed as co-presenter on the shared session "Taming 40-Minute CI" - this is expected/legitimate since he genuinely co-presents that session, not a scoping leak. No trace of Marcus's own tasks, profile, or submissions appeared, and no mention of Dana Kowalski appeared anywhere in the portal. Scoping is correctly enforced.
